News.title: Man, 48, killed & ‘several people’ rushed to hospital after car hits pedestrian – as woman, 32, arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH PROBE Man, 48, killed & ‘several people’ rushed to hospital after car hits pedestrian – as woman, 32, arrested







Next

A MAN has been killed and several others rushed to hospital after a car hit a pedestrian in a collision.

Police were called to Enfield, North London, at 12.40am on September 20, after receiving reports of a deadly crash.

Several people were rushed to hospital, but sadly a 48-year-old man – one of the passengers in the vehicle – did not survive his injuries.

His next-of-kin have been informed and are with specially trained officers.





Another passenger, a 31-year-old man, remains in hospital in a critical condition.

London Air Ambulance, Fire Brigade and Ambulance Service were all at the scene of the crash in Chase Side.

Cops arrested a 32-year-old woman on September 21 on suspicion of causing serious injury by dangerous driving and driving with a specified controlled drug above the prescribed limit.

Detective Inspector Simon Ager, from the Met’s Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “Our thoughts remain with the man’s family and loved ones as they come to terms with this devastating loss.

“We are working hard to establish the circumstances surrounding the collision and we are appealing to anyone who may have witnessed the incident to come forward.

“Any information you have could be vital in our investigation.”

Cops are urging anyone with relevant CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage to come forward.

News.title: RAF ‘terror bomb plot’ foiled by hero who saw men ‘acting suspiciously’ – before cops find vans ‘filled with explosives’
News.content:
Next

AN alleged terror plot to blow up an RAF base was foiled by a hero who saw men acting suspiciously before cops found vans filled with explosives.

Three suspicious vehicles were spotted heading through Whelford, Gloucestershire, on the way to RAF Fairford in the early hours of this morning.



A hero local living on the edge of the airbase raised the terror alarm and armed cops descended on the village.

Officers took five men into custody and bomb disposal was called in to deal with the three suspicious vans.



Explosive devices were reportedly discovered inside the vehicles.

Cops took the men into custody under the Explosives Act and further arrested them on suspicion of the preparation of a terrorist act.

The woman saw the men “hanging around“ two vans that appeared to belong to them and phoned cops to report what she had seen.

A local said: “When the cops opened up the vans they saw they were packed with explosives.



“Thank goodness this woman in the village saw what she saw and had the wit to call the cops out quickly. She may well have saved a lot of lives.

“She saw that these guys hanging around the two vans and said they were acting suspiciously and did not appear to be locals.”

A total of 85 locals were evacuated from their homes and taken to a nearby leisure centre as police set up a 400 meter cordon.

A bomb disposal robot was brought in and could be seen on aerial footage probing the rear doors of three white vans.

Large black items could be seen scattered on the floor around the vehicles in the footage.



An ongoing probe into the horrifying incident has now been taken over by counter-terror cops.

The arrested men are being held on suspicion of possessing explosives with counter-terror police receiving support in its investigation from MI5.

Counter Terrorism Policing Senior National Coordinator, Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans said: “We are in the early stages of an investigation, and five men remain in custody.



“As you would expect we are working closely with our partners to understand the circumstances of the incident.

“We continue to work with Gloucestershire Police to keep the community safe as we work to gather evidence from the scene.

“A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while the Army’s Explosive Ordinance Disposal unit conduct examinations.

“As a precaution, around 85 households have been evacuated whilst these examinations take place.”

Meanwhile, Gloucestershire Police Assistant Chief Constable Richard Ocone said: “The emergency services have well-rehearsed plans for dealing with major incidents.



“A cordon is in place as a precaution and the public can expect to see an emergency services presence in the area for some time.

“A nearby leisure centre has been opened to provide a safe space for anyone evacuated and unable to go to friends or relatives.

“We’d like to thank the residents who have left their homes this morning for their understanding and support.

“We appreciate the disruption this will have caused and would like to reassure them we are working as quickly as we can to get them back in their properties.

“We would ask the public not to speculate but to follow official channels for updates.”



Firearms officers were seen at the scene early this morning with roads leading to the nearby RAF base and the surrounding area blocked off by armed cops.

Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, and a Hazardous Area Response Team are reportedly stationed in the village of Fairford near the base.

RAF Fairford is home to the US 501st Combat Support Wing Headquarters and the 420th Air Base Squadron.



The base, which primarily houses the US Air Force, came under scrutiny in the summer after it was used to launch long-range B52 bombers for controversial strikes on Iran.

Security at the base has reportedly been significantly increased in recent days.

Roadblocks ‌and armed police prevented access and emergency vehicles remained parked nearby over the weekend, a witness claimed.

The UK said in July that its armed forces were ready to protect the country from any attack.

It followed Iran’s Revolutionary Guards warning the government not to allow US bombers to fly from England.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A US Air Force spokesperson said: “The 501st Combat Support ​Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the ​safety and security of our US service ​members, civilians, contractors, and their families.

“We ‌constantly ⁠assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and ​their families.”

News.title: Nor’easter turns deadly as man killed by tree and desperate search is launched for swimmer who vanished in 18ft waves
News.content:
Next

AT least one person has been killed as the nor’easter pummelling the East Coast turns deadly.

The monster storm which is set to continue its devastation through to Monday, has slammed the Atlantic coast with 80mph winds and 20ft waves, causing catastrophic flooding.



Over 114,000 homes have been plunged into darkness as the raging front downed power lines across New York, Connecticut, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Much of New England and the New York Tri-State Area have been brought to a standstill this weekend with huge travel disruption, major sporting and music event cancelations, and people told to stay home.





New York officials confirmed that the storm claimed its first victim on Saturday afternoon after a NYC Housing Authority worker was hit by a falling tree.

The employee, identified as 56-year-old Leighton Brown, was killed while at Cypress Hill Houses in Brooklyn, Mayor Zohran Mamdani confirmed on X.

read more on news TRAGIC TURN Student, 20, killed in horror rodeo accident in front of shocked spectators

“My thoughts are with his entire family as they deal with this unimaginable loss. May he rest in peace, and may his service to our city never be forgotten,” the mayor added.

Brown was hit at around 3:30pm and taken to Brookdale Hospital where he was pronounced dead.



A police spokesperson revealed that he had suffered “trauma throughout his body,” per The Post.

It has not been confirmed if he was working at the time of the incident.

“We are deeply saddened by this tragic loss and extend our heartfelt condolences to his family and the NYCHA community,” NYCHA said in a statement.

Two children aged 1 and 7, and two adults aged 40 and 41 suffered minor injuries when a tree fell on a playground in the Bronx at around 5:30pm.

And other tree collapses have seen some residents evacuated from their homes as a precautionary measure.



Meanwhile, a desperate search is underway off Robert Moses State Park in Long Island after a swimmer vanished as 18-foot waves crashed onto the shore.

The unidentified white male was seen in the ocean near Field #3 at around 2:30pm “when he disappeared from view and was not seen exiting the water,” New York State Police said.

He was wearing dark colored shorts and the police are seeking help from the public in identifying him.



“If anyone who has a family member, friend, or acquaintance who may have been at Robert Moses State Park during that time and whose whereabouts are currently unknown is urged to contact the New York State Police at 631-756-3300 or the New York State Park Police at 631-321-3700,” they said.

The search for the swimmer was suspended on Saturday evening as the light disappeared and is due to restart on Sunday.

According to the National Weather Service, waves at the time measured an average of 18 feet with up to 25-foot swells recorded in the ocean at times.

Swimmers and boaters were warned of the extremely hazardous water conditions with New York Governor Kathy Hochul telling people to “stay out of the water.”

“Just be smart if you live in those coastal areas,” she said in a press conference.



“Between the vicious rip currents, the heavy winds and the mammoth waves, conditions are extremely dangerous.”

“Anyone who goes in or near the water this weekend is literally gambling with their life,” she added.

The worst of the storm is set to hit on Sunday morning, with several emergency declarations still in effect.

Those in the storm’s path have been urged not to travel and to be sensible and to “stay vigilant” as some regions like New Jersey sees “some of the worst flooding” in years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Coastal flooding is being made worse by high tides and the full moon, officials warned.



“Coastal flood warnings have been issued for Atlantic City, Long Island, Norfolk, Ocean City, downtown Boston, Cape Cod, Martha’s Vineyard and Nantucket, with water levels 2‑4 feet above normal at high tide,” per The Weather Channel.

News.title: Chilling model trafficking ring where gangs lure women with warped tactics before forcing them to make sexual content
News.content:
TRAFFICKING HELL Chilling model trafficking ring where gangs lure women with warped tactics before forcing them to make sexual content







Next

DESPERATE for their big break, hundreds of aspiring models were snared by a warped trafficking ring and forced to perform sex acts on camera.

Posing as legitimate modelling agencies, ruthless criminal groups are allegedly scouting women – including Brits – with promises of lucrative work before tightening their grip and funnelling them into sexual exploitation online.



Interpol sounded the alarm this year after issuing a Purple Notice warning police forces around the world about the disturbing tactic.

The global policing giant said gangs are masquerading as legitimate modelling agencies before piling psychological pressure on recruits to produce increasingly explicit content.



In the US, hundreds of young women fell victim to an elaborate scheme tallying up to at least 573 young women and girls, according to reporting on the case.

Girls were allegedly put through gruelling, days-long sex sessions where “everything was filmed”, before the footage was turned into tapes and peddled across the globe.



Years later, the videos remain plastered across porn sites, where some victims say hundreds of men continue to watch them – while vile abuse and insults are still hurled at the women almost daily.

Mariah Rief was just 19 when she says a modelling ad plunged her into the porn industry – and within a day of applying she was allegedly put through an eight-hour sex shoot.

Desperate for cash, the Missouri-born teen had been trawling Craigslist for modelling jobs when a glossy advert showing a woman posing in a bikini caught her eye.

“Hot College Females Make 5K Cash Now (work with the best),” the banner said.



Mariah, now 29, recalls some of the ads being bizarre, with one offering: “Skydive in your bikini for like two grand.”

She told The Sun: “I just was like, ‘oh my god, I’ve never skydived before’. Look at all the weird opportunities in California that they don’t have anywhere else in the United States.”

Mariah said she replied to every advert that appeared to offer modelling work without nudity and went to sleep.



She woke to her mobile ringing and heard a New Zealand accent crackle down the line.

There was a modelling shoot. Could she be there at 2pm?

Desperate for money, Mariah climbed into her car and drove across state lines towards the coast, chasing what she believed was a modelling opportunity.

Pulling up at the address, she described being astonished at the extravagance of the Hilton San Diego Bayfront hotel in California.

She said: “It is a very, very nice hotel. When I got there, I thought, ‘I must be in the wrong place’.”



Her recruiter had told her to meet photographer Theodore Wilfred Gyi, aka Teddy, a 4ft 11 Asian man, in the hotel lobby.

During the meeting, Mariah says Teddy told her: “This is actually a really high-class, professional modelling shoot.

“Because of that, there’s a lot of money involved. So, for your anonymity and your privacy, we just got a room for paperwork.”



They made their way upstairs to the room, where she met Ruben Andre Garcia – a porn actor and producer who would eventually land himself 20 years behind bars.

It turned out Mariah had walked straight into a $17million trafficking ring creating content for a site called GirlsDoPorn.

She recalled thinking: “I don’t have a way to run. But walking through that door meant that whatever they wanted from me, they were getting it.



“I didn’t know exactly what they wanted, but I just knew that I wasn’t here for what I thought I was going to be here for.”

She added: “I even said, ‘wow, I’m a f****** idiot that can’t read an ad, I guess,’ how the heck did this happen?”

As those thoughts raced through Mariah’s mind, she said Teddy placed his hand on her lower back and whispered into her ear: “It’s probably better if you just walk in and let me explain to you what we’re going to be doing.”

Beyond the doorway, six blazing studio lights pointed towards a bed and hotness pooled her stomach.



She said: “He escorted me to the chair at the desk area.

“I remember thinking, ‘I’m going to lose my f****** mind’. I was afraid that if I lost my mind, somebody was going to get really hurt. I was terrified.”

A long, complicated-looking contract was placed beside a Bank of America envelope stuffed with a $4,500 wad of cash.

“Just sign it,” she claims Teddy said, promising her the content they were about to force her into producing would never appear on the internet.



He allegedly told her: “It’s going to only be made and put on DVDs for rich, white men in Australia.”

That promise would later be shattered when the group shared her videos with friends and family through Facebook in a sick attempt to drive more internet traffic.

Mariah said: “I remember begging myself to just go numb – just normalise whatever this is, and you have the highest chance of getting out alive.”

Dissociating as she tried to piece together what was happening, Mariah signed the contract without being able to bring herself to read its contents.

She then forced herself towards the bathroom and knocked on the door to find Andre Garcia standing there.



Mariah said: “He was naked with just a towel wrapped around his waist, he was probably 6ft 2ins, with a slender man physique.”

After that, Mariah says she was forced into having sex with Garcia for eight hours that day with only a minute break between each round.

The team brought in make-up artists allegedly from major make-up brands, Mariah said, while clothes from huge fashion labels were provided for the girls to dress up and be glammed up for the porn shoots.

Mariah endured years of harassment over the videos, which left a stain across the internet, before the FBI eventually contacted her and identified her as a victim of a wider trafficking ring.



She has now become a prominent campaigner against the online afterlife of sexual exploitation – recently winning a case for the girls to own the rights for all the content.

Seven conspirators were sentenced for their involvement in GirlsDoPorn, with the ringleader Michael Pratt receiving the heaviest punishment – 27 years behind bars.

For more than three years Pratt remained on the run, eventually earning a place on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted list before police tracked him down in Spain in 2022.

The content creator, Theodore Gyi, was sentenced to four years for his role in the sex-trafficking operation.



For years, Pratt and his conspirators preyed on young women who thought they were answering modelling adverts, prosecutors found, before using deception and pressure to get them in front of a camera.

Hundreds of young women fell victim to the elaborate scheme tallying up to at least 573 young women and girls, according to reporting on the case.

An FBI officer confirmed to Mariah that some of those victims included British girls.

She said: “There are lot’s of US victims in every state, but there’s also victims in the UK, Brazil, and Canada.”

Nitzia, from the US, was also a teen who fell victim to fake ads and found herself talking to a polished recruiter named “Jonathan”.



Over the following months, the stranger slowly became familiar as emails turned into phone calls and plans were made for Nitzia to travel from Sacramento to San Diego for work.

Shortly after turning 18, she boarded a plane, believing she was flying towards a modelling opportunity.

After landing in San Diego, Nitzia was collected from the airport by Valorie Moser and driven to a hotel, where the glamorous opportunity she had travelled hundreds of miles to pursue quickly began to unravel.



Valorie was later sentenced to two years in prison for her involvement with the sex trafficking conspiracy.

There was no modelling shoot waiting for her and she instead discovered that the people she had trusted wanted her to appear in a pornographic video for GirlsDoPorn.

Barely an adult, far from home and surrounded by strangers, Nitzia said she became frightened about what could happen if she refused and felt she had little choice but to comply.

She recalled being given alcohol and drugs before being told to “calm down”.

In a blur, Nitzia’s signature was scribbled onto the confusing paperwork, signing away her body to the sex trade.



Like Mariah, Nitzia was told her videos would only be sold to overseas collectors.

But the clips were uploaded online and pushed onto major pornography sites.

The company allegedly went out of their way to advertise the content to the girls’ friends, families and employers in a twisted bid to generate more web traffic.

The man Nitzia knew as “Jonathan” was Andre Garcia – the man Mariah was forced to have sex with and one of the operation’s lead recruiters.

Authorities said the conspirators would threaten the women with lawsuits or leave them fearing they would have to pay for their own flights home.



Alexandra Foster, a Department of Justice attorney who helped prosecute the case said: “There obviously was coercion and sometimes force, but really these women had been lied to at the front end.”

Yet for survivors, a prison door slamming shut did not make the videos disappear.

Although the GirlsDoPorn proceedings ended this year, survivors say the fallout hasn’t.

Videos of their abuse have continued to circulate online on sites in places like China and Russia.

Nitzia and Mariah have both spoken of cyberstalkers sending intimidating messages and publishing her personal information online.



According to both Nitzia and Rief, more than a dozen survivors in the GirlsDoPorn case have died from suicide, drug overdose and domestic violence. Others, including Nitzia, have made suicide attempts.

The Sun has not been able to independently verify these claims.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Sun has reached out to Craigslist and The Hilton hotel for comment.

News.title: Moment pensioner, 80, deliberately destroys driveway fence with 2 different cars in bitter neighbour row over oil spill
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a pensioner, 80, deliberately destroys a driveway fence with his car in a bitter neighbour row over an oil spill.

Peter Ellis has been fined £1,630 and banned from contacting his neighbour for a year after the furious dispute escalated.



The OAP was captured on CCTV footage ramming his red Land Rover into his neighbour’s white fence several times.

Video shows Ellis behind the wheel of his motor lining up the ramming manoeuvre.



He then accelerates and smashes into the fence with the red vehicle before reversing and going for a second hit.

The panelling on the plastic fence collapses with pieces of it falling to the floor.



Ellis then parks the Land Rover next to the fence before climbing out and admiring the damage he caused.

A second video shows the fence partially repaired as Ellis arrives again in the red Land Rover.



For a second time the OAP rams the fence with his large motor, causing the semi-repaired structure to collapse.

Later footage shows the 80-year-old looking at the partially destroyed fencing before climbing into a black Volvo.

He then reverses the motor from its parking spot next to the fence, turning as he does and smashing into the fence again.

On Monday, September 14, Ellis was dragged to Brighton Magistrates’ Court.

The court heard that Ellis, of Bishopstone, East Sussex, had hit his neighbour John Rowe’s fence an estimated 20 times across just four months.



District Judge Hawgood found the octogenarian guilty of criminal damage – saying he had deliberately tried to “annoy and frustrate” his neighbour.

The court heard the pair had been neighbours for some time and, at one point, had been friendly with each other.

They had even pooled their money together to tarmac the driveway between the two properties.

But things turned sour when Ellis accidentally spilled hydraulic oil on the driveway as he fixed a puncture on his car.

This led Rowe to install a plastic fence to mark off his side of the drive.



Giving evidence, Rowe, who chose to appear behind a screen, said he had told Ellis of his intention to install the fence.

He added that Ellis had told him “put the damn fence up then” – though Rowe admitted erecting the fence was against a covenant.

Ellis, representing himself in court, said he was unable to see the fence when he was in the drivers’ seat of the car due to the incline of the driveway – and that hitting it had been an accident.

He also said the fence was very delicate, adding: “It is so fragile, it is an ornament not a fence.

“A breeze of wind could blow it away.”



District Judge Hawgood found Ellis guilty on the charge of criminal damage, stating that if he was capable of using the driveway without hitting the fence it must have been intentional.

In a victim impact statement read by the prosecution, Mr Rowe said that the incident meant himself and his wife could not fully enjoy their retirement.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

District Judge Hawgood told Ellis he must pay £980 in compensation and also imposed a restraining order not to contact Mr Rowe directly or indirectly for 12 months.

He must also pay court costs of £650.

News.title: Putin’s granddaughter, 8, ‘given mother’s family name to avoid being a Zelensky’ as child’s luxury life revealed
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

SURNAME SWITCH Putin’s granddaughter, 8, ‘given mother’s family name to avoid being a Zelensky’ as child’s luxury life revealed







Next

VLADIMIR Putin’s granddaughter was given her mum’s family name to avoid sharing surnames with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky, reports say.

Eight-year-old Elsa, whose dad has the same second name as Putin’s mortal enemy, is also treated like Russian royalty, according to local media.



The young girl was born to Putin’s daughter Katerina Tikhonova, 40, and Igor Zelensky – a 57-year-old ballet star with no relation whatsoever to the Ukrainian leader.

Elsa is believed to have been named after Princess Elsa from the popular animated film Frozen, Russian media reports.



Local outlet Proekt said Katerina gave her daughter the first name due to her love of Hollywood.

If the young girl had taken her father’s last name, she would have been called Elsa Zelenskaya – the female form of Zelensky.



Elsa has never been pictured publicly due to high security surrounding her identity.

The child’s name was reportedly discovered while the Russian outlet was analysing a leaked database from the Kremlin’s Federal Border Service.



The Russian despot’s own daughter was born Katerina Putina.

But she has also used a different surname – Tikhonova – for many years to avoid links to her father.

Leaked records show Elsa first travelled outside Russia by private jet with her parents on November 11, 2019, shortly before her second birthday.



The family spent two months in Munich, where her dad Igor was working as an artistic director with the Bavarian State Ballet.

At least four nannies, two foreign language tutors, her mum’s assistant, and Federal Protective Service (FSO) officers, reportedly accompanied them on the lavish trip.

Elsa’s next journey abroad was to Croatia, reports say.

Putin has never publicly confirmed Katerina’s identity as his daughter.

But several investigations by major international outlets and sanctions imposed by Western governments have pointed to this being the case.



Once a rock’n’roll dancer, Katerina now heads Innopraktika, a state-backed technology and development organisation linked to Moscow State University.

She was previously married to Russia’s youngest billionaire Kirill Shamalov, 44, son of a close Putin crony.

Katerina has an older sister, Maria Vorontsova, 41.

She was born from Putin’s marriage to his own ex-wife Lyudmila Ocheretnaya, 68, Russia’s former first lady.

They are only slightly younger than Putin’s partner Alina Kabaeva, 43, with whom he has two young sons.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Putin also has two grandchildren from Vorontsova, including a half-Dutch grandson.

Katerina also has a younger half-sister, Luiza Rozova, 23, from Putin’s extra-marital relationship with Svetlana Krivinogikh, 51.

News.title: Inside prison life of Angel of Death killer Beverly Allitt – from self-harm stunts to dark facade and staff manipulation
News.content:
TWISTED NURSE Inside prison life of Angel of Death killer Beverly Allitt – from self-harm stunts to dark facade and staff manipulation







Next

SHE is the killer nurse who became infamous long before Lucy Letby was jailed.

Beverly Allitt murdered four children, attempted to kill another three and hurt a further six. Now The Sun can reveal details of the twisted monster’s life inside high-security psychiatric hospital Rampton.



We tell how the Angel of Death has spent decades trying to self-harm so she can get back into a hospital – years after stalking babies on the children’s ward at Grantham and Kesteven Hospital in Lincolnshire.

The 57-year-old was diagnosed with Munchausen syndrome by proxy – a condition where someone harms others to get attention – after being convicted of her heinous crimes.



A source told The Sun: “She acts like the model prisoner and is always compliant and never complaining but there’s always that darkness about her.

“She has to be heavily supervised because she has a history of trying to hurt herself to get a trip to A&E. In the past she’s tried to swallow tiny bits of glass and poured boiling water on hands.

“It’s like she just can’t stop and see what she’s done to those poor babies and families – everything is about her.

“She will never, ever leave Rampton and I think she knows that.”



The case shares striking similarities with that of Lucy Letby, 36, who is serving 15 whole-life sentences for killing seven babies and attempting to murder seven more at the Countess of Chester Hospital.

Letby was accused of injecting air and insulin into her victims but has always maintained her innocence as MPs, doctors and top lawyers fight to get her convictions overturned.

An exclusive Sun documentary by investigations editor Rob Pattinson reveals new details that cast doubt on her conviction.

There was never any doubt over the guilt of Allitt, whose victims were aged seven weeks to 11-years-old.



She now spends her days at Rampton either in her own room, at arts and crafts classes or at one-on-one therapy and counselling sessions.

The senior detective who nailed the killer told The Sun how she is a master of manipulation who once exploited staff at Rampton so much that bosses changed shift rotas to throw her off.

Retired detective superintendent Stuart Clifton, who led the investigation into the hospital murders, said: “When Allitt first went to Rampton she was manipulating staff all the time, so much so that they had to change shift patterns.

“I never found out exactly how she was doing it but I’d imagine she became very friendly with staff to get her own way, sending them off on errands for blankets and the like so she could be alone.



“I’m not shocked to hear she has tried to self harm over the years. Her history from being small was all about getting attention. As a child, if she had a sprained wrist, she’d insist on a sling, that sort of thing. She wanted to be sick so was the focus of attention.

“She spent a lot of time lying too. She fibbed to people that her parents had split up and she’d had to live with an aunt in Cornwall. She also claimed to have played squash for Lincolnshire. It was a pattern set at a young age. It was anything for a bit of attention.

“When she was arrested she also developed anorexia and turned up at court several stone lighter through not eating. It was an another example of her trying to keep control.”

Alllitt was a trainee nurse when she was given a six month contract at the Lincolnshire hospital in 1991.



She had only just scraped through training and before and during her crimes was regularly attending the casualty department of the same hospital with repeated episodes of self-injury.

Over a period of 59 days from February 1991, four babies died after being brought to Ward Four, where Allitt worked, They went into the hospital with minor complaints like chest infections and gastroenteritis.

A further nine collapsed after the nurse injected syringes full of insulin or potassium chloride into their bodies, but were resuscitated by doctors.

Allitt was jailed for a minimum of 30 years but was transferred to Rampton within weeks.



She has spent the past five years appealing to get back into a mainstream prison where she can apply for parole – a move that isn’t possible in psychiatric care.

At her trial in 1993, Allitt pleaded not guilty, putting her victim’s family through torment as they were forced to hear details of how thier children died.

Four months later she finally confessed her crimes to detective Stuart Clifton during a meeting with her lawyer.

The ex-policeman said: “She turned to me and said, ‘I only did nine’.

“She wouldn’t admit the others and I think she denied one because she was still in touch with the family after becoming Godmother to their child.



“She refused to put any detail on it. I wanted her to tell me precisely what she’d done and she walked away.”

Allitt later wrote a letter to the Home Office, admitting all the attacks, including those on nine-week-old twins Becky and Katie Phillips.

Becky was admitted to Ward Four for a stomach bug in April 1991 and died at home two days later after being given an insulin overdose by Allitt, who gave her sister Katie the same drug along with potassium.



She also tried to smother the tiny baby leaving her paralysed but the Phillips family had no idea the nurse was behind it all and made her Katie’s godmother.

After conviction, it emerged that, as a child, Allitt would fake illness and wear bandages. It’s said she even convinced a doctor to remove her appendix by feigning pain.

Former detective Clifton revealed Allitt showed bizarre behaviours while sharing accommodation with other nurses – and how she frightened a family who took her in when she was on bail.

He said: “When she was a trainee nurse living with other staff strange things happened, faeces were found in the fridge and curtains were set on fire.

“They could never prove it was Allitt but she was always at the centre of the drama.



“When she was on bail after first being arrested, the family of a boyfriend took her into their home in Peterborough and she claimed there was a poltergeist in the house.

Who were Allitt's victims? Allitt killed four children while working on Ward Four. Liam Taylor

Allitt’s first victim was seven week old Liam Taylor, who was admitted with a chest infection.

He began to improve after being given antibiotics but, after his parents were sent home to rest, he mysteriously took a turn for the worse.

Doctors were only alerted to his worsening condition by Allitt, despite the baby being hooked up to alarms to monitor his breathing and oxygen levels.

He was put on life support but died of a heart attack in his mum’s arms the next day.

Consultants on the ward were confused by Liam’s dramatic relapse and questioned why the alarms didn’t sound in time.

Timothy Hardwick

Timothy Hardwick, 11, had cerebral palsy and was admitted to the ward after suffering an epileptic seizure.

He fell asleep, with his breathing and heart rate stable, but just 30 minutes later Allitt raised the alarm that he was dying.

Attempts to re-start his heart were made but he died on March 5, 1991.

Becky & Katie Phillips

Becky Phillips, two months old, was admitted to the ward for gastroenteritis on April 1, 1991.

She was given an insulin overdose by Allitt and died at home two days later.

Doctors were concerned that whatever had caused Becky’s death could also affect her identical twin Katie, so she was admitted to hospital for monitoring.

This genuine concern actually put Katie in harm’s way and in direct contact with Allitt.

Within hours, the nurse attempted to kill Katie four times by suffocation and injections of insulin and potassium.

Katie was put on life support, suffered epileptic fits and was eventually transferred to Queen’s Medical Centre, away from the nurse who had attempted to kill her.

She was left epileptic and paralysed as a result of Allitt’s actions.

Claire Peck

Claire Peck, 15 months, was admitted to the ward after suffering an asthma attack on April 22, 1991.

After being put on a ventilator, she was left in Allitt’s care and then went into cardiac arrest.

She was resuscitated but died after a second episode of cardiac arrest – during an interval when she was left alone with Allitt again.

The toddler became the fourth child to die on the ward in two months. Allitt’s surviving victims included 15-month-old Kayley Asher, who suffered brain injuries, five-year-old Bradley Gibson who was given an insulin dose during treatment for pneumonia and five-month old Paul Crampton who was saved from the nurse after being transferred to another hospital following a series of collapses.

“Bleach was tipped onto a bed and the curtains were again set on fire. She was very, very strange.”

Ex-policeman Clifton believes that Allitt, the daughter of a wine merchant dad and school cleaner mum, is once again manipulating staff to try and get into a mainstream jail.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She applied for a move in 2021 and 2023 but was refused by a medical panel.

Clifton said: “I don’t think she ever realised that going into a hospital environment would mean she couldn’t apply for parole but I don’t think she will ever be released.”

News.title: Stag-do hotspot torn apart by warring drug gangs with brutal slayings in cafes… & innocent victims caught in crossfire
News.content:
Next

PACKED with Brit tourists, this European coastal city is known for its sun- drenched beaches and legendary stag night scene with raucous parties of grooms-to-be flocking there in their thousands.

But a vicious settling of scores has erupted between two notorious drug trafficking gangs – transforming this holiday hotspot into the latest battleground of a brutal war that has left a grim trail of blood across Europe.



Now experts warn tourists could be dragged into the crossfire as brazen executions spill out onto the streets of the popular Spanish city.



A recent spate of broad daylight shootings in Barcelona have been linked to a raging conflict of revenge between two Balkan crime gangs.

Carles Fiexa, Social Anthropology Professor at Pompeu Fabra University in Barcelona, told The Sun: “These are criminal organisations that have established relationships with Mexican cartels.

“They are not juvenile gangs – they’re structured according to the mafia model.”

In the latest attack, on June 10, when a man was shot at point-blank range in the back of the head in the affluent “Hollywood Hills” suburb, Sant Gervasi-Galvany.

Just a 30 minute walk from Sagrada Família – Barcelona’s biggest tourist attraction – the killing took place on the morning of Pope Leo XIV’s visit to the city.



Three days earlier a Serbian man was shot several times in the back with an automatic rifle at around 9pm in Calle Mineria, Zona Franca.

And in April, two men dressed in black opened fire on a man sat outside a café with a woman and child in Barcelona’s Poblenou neighbourhood.

Four out of five shots hit the man who fell to the floor with blood gushing from his wounds. An innocent woman passing by on the street suffered a chest wound.



In an update police said the unidentified woman had recovered.

Chris Dalby, Head of Intelligence at Dyami Security Intelligence, said: “Balkan organised crime networks have been deeply involved in the European cocaine trade for years, and Spain has long been an important operating environment for them.

“What is changing now is the visibility of the violence.”

Authorities suspect the three killings to be linked to a Europe-wide war between two Balkan crime clans – the Škaljari and their Kavač rivals.

The Kavač and Škaljari hail from Kotor, a city on Montenegro’s picturesque Adriatic coast.



The Kavač and Škaljari were once part of the same organisation smuggling drugs from South America into Europe.

But the gangs split in 2014 after a 200kg cocaine deal went bad in the Spanish coastal city of Valencia – sparking a bloody battle.

That split developed into “one of Europe’s most persistent organised-crime vendettas”, Chris said.



The raging war between the two clans is estimated to have claimed the lives of at least 80 people across the continent.

Shootings, explosives, sniper attacks and contract killings have been linked to the conflict in Montenegro, Serbia, Greece, Austria and Turkey.

But the Catalan capital has become their latest battleground.

The man killed outside a cafe in April was later identified as Krsto “The Terminator” Vujić – an alleged member of the Škaljari crime clan.

He was reportedly on trial in absentia in Montenegro for his alleged involvement in the murder of a Kavač member.



Barcelona is just “one node” in an international conflict that moves with the people involved, Chris said.

“Their members can operate in Barcelona, move money through another country, obtain cocaine through contacts in Latin America and have associates elsewhere in Europe”, he added.

The rapid rise in violence could be linked to the two clans now vying for control over Barcelona’s cocaine market.

Chris said: “The cocaine business requires ports, warehouses, transport, legitimate companies, intermediaries, property, money laundering and connections into the wider European market. Barcelona has all of those.”

Barcelona’s thriving tourism industry also provides a source of recreational drug consumption.



Professor Carles said: “Those benefits justify the risk.

“There is no data to show that they have settled in Catalonia permanently.

“But there is certainly a change in the trafficking routes from America and North Africa, which no longer arrive through Galicia in small boats.



“They have diversified their modes of transport, using the ports of the Mediterranean.”

A spate of attacks erupted in July 2025 – leaving three of four targets dead.

Filip Knežević, an alleged Kavač member, was gunned down while entering his apartment building in Barcelona’s Eixample district.

He was wanted in Serbia for allegedly killing two Škaljari members on the Greek island of Corfu in 2020.

Just over two weeks later, on August 2, another alleged Škaljari named Predrag Vujošević was shot in central Barcelona. He is the only one of four victims of attacks that month to survive.



The next victim was Milan Milić, also allegedly part of the Škaljari clan, according to police.

He was shot and killed on December 22, in Castelldefels, a municipality close to Barcelona.

Chris said there is an “intimidation element” to the brazen attacks.

“But I am more concerned by the increased availability of firearms within sections of the European cocaine economy”, he added.

“That is one of the areas where European law enforcement is losing a march on organized crime.”



While the attacks are “overwhelmingly” targeted assassinations, the public nature of violence could leave residents and tourists exposed.

Chris said: “There is no indication that tourists or ordinary Barcelona residents are being or will be deliberately targeted by Balkan criminal organisations.

“But If somebody opens fire on a person sitting on a terrace, walking along a pavement or entering an apartment building, everybody nearby is potentially exposed.”

It comes as experts warn that Spain is emerging as a haven for drug trafficking and violence.

The country acts as the gateway to Europe for the international drug trade, where global cartels from South America, the Balkans, and North Africa collaborate



The latest report by the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) marked up Barcelona as the continent’s cocaine capital – recording an astonishing 185 per cent increase in cocaine use compared to 2024.

This was followed by the Spanish city of Lleida, which recorded a 125 per cent increase.

Chris said: “Spain is unquestionably one of the most important cocaine entry points in Europe – and it has a serious organised crime problem.

“There is money laundering, firearms violence and an enormous amount of criminal money moving through the legal economy.”

Enforcing ports is a crucial part of dismantling the work of these criminal syndicates.



“Criminal organisations only need to corrupt a very small number of people inside enormous logistical systems to move extraordinary quantities of drugs”, Chris said.

In January Spanish cops pulled off the biggest cocaine seizure ever made at sea, intercepting a cargo ship carrying almost 10 tonnes of cocaine.

Chris said: “Spain is conducting major seizures, dismantling criminal networks, arresting senior traffickers, prosecuting offenders and cooperating extensively with police in Latin America and elsewhere in Europe.

“If Spain were to begin a real measured crackdown on not just drugs, but financial flows, front companies, dismantling entire networks, we could see criminals shift elsewhere.

“That means protecting port and logistics workers from recruitment and intimidation, identifying insider corruption, improving container intelligence, tracking money into property and legitimate companies, confiscating criminal assets, targeting weapons suppliers and investing heavily in cooperation with Latin American authorities.”

News.title: Burnham proposes NHS-style social care system for England
News.content:
Andy Burnham wants to offer access to free social care services to everyone in England, and will put his plans before voters at the next general election.

The prime minister told the BBC that it would be a system in which "everyone contributes, everyone is covered". He did not rule out tax rises, acknowledging it may be "difficult or unpopular" with some.

Burnham said he wants to set out his "vision" on Tuesday and Whitehall troubleshooter Baroness Casey, who is conducting a review, will advise on the "best way of doing it".

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said the PM was suggesting Labour wanted "more tax rises" to pay for the reforms, adding the Conservatives would not support this.

Burnham has made reforming social care one of his flagship policies and has spoken of the experience of his father Roy, who had Alzheimer's and died earlier this month.

While he has been clear on his ambition to make changes to the system, he has yet to explain how any changes would be funded.

Adult social care provides state support to help people live more independently, including assistance at home.

Unlike the NHS, social care is not free at the point of use. In England and Northern Ireland, people with savings worth more than Â£23,250 are not entitled to help with care costs from their council.

In Wales and Scotland, different rules apply in terms of eligibility.

Speaking to the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, the prime minister said: "I am talking about a system that works on NHS principles because that is the only way you can make it work.

"There is free personal care elsewhere in the UK. I don't think it's right that people in England don't get the same and it's not something we're going to rush."

Personal care offered in Scotland is available to all adults who are assessed as needing help with tasks including eating and bathing.

News.title: 'Broken social care will in the end break the NHS,' says Burnham
News.content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has proposed a national care service, free at the point of use, to tackle England's "threadbare" social care services.

In an interview with BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, the prime minister said "broken social care will in the end break the NHS" and that he would not look in the other direction.

Burnham went on to say that he will develop a clear plan for a new national care service that is then put to the public at the next general election.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp, who also spoke to Kuenssberg, warned that "more tax rises" are likely planned to fund the scheme, which is a "red line" for the Conservatives

Read more here.

News.title: Ten NHS staff removed over Noah Woods data breach
News.content:
Ten NHS staff have been removed from duty or suspended after a data breach involving the digital medical records of three-year-old Noah Woods.

Launching an "urgent" investigation, Dr Martin Mansfield, deputy chief medical officer at East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust, said that any unauthorised access of patient data was "completely unacceptable".

The trust has apologised "unreservedly" to Noah's family and said disciplinary action would be taken if needed.

A major search for Noah was carried out in the village of Brantham, Suffolk, after the child went missing on 15 September. His body was found the next day in a nearby pond by police divers.

A spokesperson for the trust said 10 employees had been "removed from active duty or suspended whilst investigations are concluded".

It comes after Sir Jim Mackey, the chief executive of NHS England, wrote to every trust on Friday, ordering stronger measures to tackle data breaches.

"We have seen too many cases of people abusing that trust, and enough is enough," said Sir Jim.

"Anyone who thinks they can satisfy their curiosity by looking at a patient's record should know this: they will be found out, they may lose their career and could end up with a criminal record."

News.title: Celebrity Traitors 2 cast: Who are this year's 'big dogs' and dark horses?
News.content:
If Carr was the star of last year's show, then perhaps his fellow TV funnymen could be the ones to watch this time around.

Naturally good readers of a room and skilled at misdirection, comedians can inject some comic relief into those tense roundtable moments.

It worked for Carr, who was considered to be less of a threat and more out of his depth by the other sleuths.

This time around, stand-up star Joe Lycett, 38, is one of the leading candidates for the role of class clown. Known for his quick wit and political stunts, Lycett told the BBC he asked Carr for advice on "how to spot a rotten little traitor like you".

Last year's winner replied: "Just anyone that's sweating and giggling."

With his brightly coloured outfits, Lycett will bring some glamour to the castle, if and when he's not donning the famous dark cloak.

"There's a lot of variety and silly stuff that I might not get to wear at all if I end up doing a Paloma," he noted, with reference to Paloma Faith, who was brutally killed off early doors last year by her supposed friend, Carr.

If laughing all the way to the winning line is to work again, then it's hard to look beyond James Acaster.

Anyone who has seen his Netflix special Repertoire or heard his podcast Off Menu will know his deadpan, absurdist humour and whimsical flights of fancy could make it difficult to tell whether he is telling the truth or not.

A "huge fan" of the show since the first non-celebrity edition in 2022, Acaster, 41, said he would prefer to be a faithful as he wasn't good at lying - though Carr did previously say something similar...

News.title: Big Bang wins over fans old and new at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium
News.content:
A sea of glowing yellow crowns. Thousands of voices chanting in Korean.

An explosive surge of energy as the opening synth riffs of Fantastic Baby shatter the stadium air. Big Bang is back.

Fourteen years after their first major European shows, and after a decade marked by military service, member departures and legal scandals, the South Korean group played at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Saturday as part of their 20th anniversary world tour.

Inside the near-capacity venue, the crowd did not just watch a concert - they stepped into a significant moment in K-pop history.

As the band emerged in their trademark high-fashion, glittering outfits, the crowd danced freely, setting the tone for an evening that felt less like a routine tour stop and more like a homecoming.

News.title: Why families are being urged to look closer on autumn walks
News.content:
From fairytale toadstools to fungi that look like birds' nests, experts say some of Britain's most unusual mushrooms are beginning to emerge as autumn arrives.

Hidden in parks, woodlands and nature reserves, species ranging from the bright-red fly agaric to the rare red cage fungus can be found by anyone willing to slow down and take a closer look.

For James Benwell, of the Birmingham and Black Country Wildlife Trust, searching for fungi has become a way to explore the outdoors with his young son.

He said mushroom spotting can transform an ordinary walk into an adventure, revealing colourful and unusual species that many people pass by without noticing.

Across the West Midlands, fungi enthusiasts have recorded everything from tiny bird's nest fungi in Birmingham city centre, to fly agaric mushrooms growing beneath woodland birch trees and a rare red cage fungus discovered in Cannon Hill Park.

Many species can go unnoticed among fallen leaves, rotting wood and the bases of trees, but Benwell said taking the time to look more closely opens up a hidden world.

"Every walk becomes interesting and exciting if you're exploring and if you're looking for new things," he said.

News.title: China's new youth idol isn't a pop star - he's an academic
News.content:
"A star sent from the heavens," is how Zihan Han describes the man she's become a huge fan of recently, a man who young Chinese people call an "idol".

Except this is no pop singer or movie star, but a 54-year old anthropologist. Professor Biao Xiang has become an unlikely guide for an increasingly disillusioned generation.

And it's because of what he talks about: anxiety and how to navigate it.

China's economy and tech have grown at breakneck speed, but there is plenty worrying its Gen Z, from jobs to romantic prospects to the sheer pressure of keeping up.

"The transition from school to the real world brings a lot of uncertainty now, and people often feel anxious because they don't know how to face it," says a 23-year-old Chinese graduate who didn't want to reveal her name because she was worried speaking to foreign media might affect her chances of finding a job back home.

"People need an anchor in their life. And his words make us feel there is someone that gets me."

She and Zihan were among some 500 people - mostly Chinese diaspora - who piled into an auditorium recently in Singapore. Xiang spoke for more than an hour in Mandarin before he took questions. When it ended, dozens queued to meet and take photos with him. The Chinese grad called it "an academic fan meeting".

Xiang has been interviewed by major Chinese outlets and has travelled to top Chinese campuses to talk, including at his alma mater, the prestigious Peking University â one talk earlier this year was live-streamed because the auditorium was full. "When in doubt, ask Biao Xiang," has become a saying, according to Chinese media.

News.title: White casts doubt on Fury-Joshua after 24 hours of chaos
News.content:
Two days after the announcement British boxing had waited a decade for, Dana White - the UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief named as one of the figures promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua - was asked whether the fight would actually happen.

"I don't know," he said.

White was speaking at London's Copper Box on Saturday, where British heavyweight Johnny Fisher beat Michael Pirotton on his Zuffa Boxing debut. But for much of the media in attendance another heavyweight fight dominated the evening.

Asked whether Wednesday's scheduled Fury-Joshua news conference in London would take place, White added: "I have no idea."

On Thursday, Fury and Joshua were officially announced to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, live globally on Netflix. By Friday, that certainty had unravelled.

A dispute over who is entitled to promote the event led to claims of contractual breaches, talk of possible replacement fights and another flurry of cryptic social-media posts.

Even by boxing's recent standards, the past 24 hours have been extraordinary - and not a particularly flattering look for the sport.

News.title: Thousands without water and roads closed after burst pipe
News.content:
Thousands of homes in parts of West Sussex have water supply issues and a number of roads have flooded after what police are describing as a "significant" leak.

Roads around the Southgate Roundabout in Crawley have been closed on Sunday morning due to the burst water pipe, Sussex Police said.

Southern Water said around 9,000 customers were impacted and it was setting up bottled water stations.

A company spokesperson said: "Our teams are on site and working as quickly and safely as possible to repair the burst and restore supplies."

The company said customers were experiencing a loss of water supply or low pressure in the following areas - Woolborough Road, Holmcroft, Southgate, Tilgate and Furnace Green.

It reported at 12:00 BST that supplies had returned to some homes.

The Southern Water spokesperson added: "Restoring water to customers as quickly as possible remains our highest priority."

John Boulton, who is 82, and his partner are without water.

He said: "It's pretty disgusting, really - we pay so much for the water supply."

Boulton said he had just paid Â£22 for bottled water in a shop.

News.title: Murder probe as cyclist dies following moped crash
News.content:
A murder inquiry has begun after an e-bike cyclist died following a collision with a moped in west London.

Emergency services were called to North Pole Road, North Kensington, at about 01:20 BST on Friday where the seriously injured 24-year-old man was found. He was pronounced dead at the scene shortly after.

Police said the investigation was at an early stage but it was believed the moped had been pursuing the e-bike cyclist prior to the crash.

Dt Ch Insp Neil John said detectives were "pursuing a number of lines of inquiry, including efforts to identify and trace the rider of the moped".

"Our thoughts are with the victim's family at what is a very difficult time," he added.

"We have launched a full investigation and are working hard to get answers and establish exactly what happened.

"As part of this, we're urging anyone who was in the area at the time and may have seen the e-bike or the moped to get in touch with us as soon as possible. If you have any information that could help, please come forward."

News.title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos
News.content:
Traitors star Paul Gorton did not think twice about sharing photographs on social media while enjoying a family holiday with his wife and two young children.

But when he returned home he discovered that his house in Cheshire had been burgled just days earlier.

"The eerie bit is at 21:10 BST I posted that me and Kate were by the side of the pool, we've got full bellies, the kids are in bed, we're actually having our little bit of the holiday," he said.

"About 20 minutes later, little did we know, our house has been broken into."

Paul's bike as well as several sentimental items including an irreplaceable ring from Kate's grandmother were stolen in the burglary on 28 August.

The perpetrators managed to break in through the bi-fold doors at the back of the house by using a technique known as lock snapping before cutting the broadband connection.

News.title: Man charged with murdering woman in Darlington
News.content:
A man has been charged with murdering a woman who was found dead by police.

Andrew Bell, 44, of Darlington, is accused of killing Leanne Park, 44, in the town on Wednesday.

Durham Police said she was pronounced dead at an address in Parkgate at about 21:15 BST. Her family said she was the "best mam, nana, daughter and friend we could wish for".

Bell is due to appear at Newton Aycliffe Magistrates' Court on Monday.

A 27-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender has been released on bail, the force said.

A spokesperson said crime scene investigators would continue to work at the scene and a police cordon was "expected to remain in place for some time".

Anyone with information about the murder is urged to contact detectives.

News.title: Gaming pays me double what I earned as a teacher
News.content:
In 2019, Jarvs Tasker was forced to give up her teaching career due to chronic illness when she was just 28.

Fast forward seven years, and she earns double her former annual salary, running Jarvs Indie Insights, which provides communication and marketing within the gaming industry.

She visited the University of Suffolk's e-sport building in Ipswich to celebrate independent game developers and studios on Wednesday.

"I can comfortably say it probably would have taken me about 20 years in teaching to earn what I make now," she said.

When Tasker left teaching, she initially started volunteering for PlayStation's YouTube channel, but she said there was lots of crossover between the two industries.

"Managing a community is very similar to managing a class of kids, so there's a lot of crossover skills there, but actually, video games is one of those industries where a lot of people come into it later on in life."

Tasker, who lives in Exeter, believed young people might not know the "many pathways" available in the industry.

"The video games community is very strong, and they will champion people that love what they do, but they'll also notice if you're in it just for the money," she continued.

"Passion is the most important thing."

Asked about the impact of AI, she said she believed the industry was doing a "really great job" at rejecting it, because players hated it.

"I think as an industry we should be really proud of the fact that we're still championing human creativity and that the audience is also on board with that," she added.

News.title: Child's hidden letter found after 44 years
News.content:
A letter written by a 10-year-old girl in the 1980s and hidden in the cavity of the stairs at her home has been found 44 years later.

The house in Hockley, Essex, was undergoing renovation work when a worker found the scrap of paper and passed it to Michelle Harwood, who now lives there.

Filled with curiosity, the 36-year-old charity worker examined it - noting "really neat" handwriting for a child - and posted on her local Facebook community group on Thursday morning to track down the author.

Within an hour, multiple people had found and tagged Rachel Miles, now a 54-year- old teacher in Milton Keynes, Buckinghamshire. And she responded.

News.title: 'I was angry at my husband - I didn't know he had dementia'
News.content:
Since Clive's death in 1999, Helen has been working as a dementia researcher, raising awareness of his condition and continuing his legacy through her charity, The Clive Project.

She continues to tell her story because there is still "more to be done" to help dementia patients and their families, she said.

Helen described her late-husband as a calm, level-headed and "very active guy" who used to run marathons, even "before it was popular".

"Clive was unflappable," she said.

"He reckoned he failed if he lost his temper."

But as Clive approached his 40s things began to change.

"You can't really tell at what stage somebody's behaviour changes," she said.

"Younger people in particular are always going to be difficult to diagnose.

"And he covered up some things. He never admitted to me that he was having problems with reading and writing."

While Helen had never before heard of dementia in younger people, she said she "knew there was something wrong".

"I would make plans and he would forget he was looking after the children," she said.

"We had very many arguments about it.

"He said, 'I'm just growing old' - and he was early forties then."

News.title: Your pictures of the Harvest Moon shimmering across the UK sky
News.content:
September's full Moon glowed across the UK sky on Saturday and many people seemed to have perfect conditions for viewing it.

It's also known as the Harvest Moon because of its association with the time of year people traditionally gather crops.

The Moon reached its fullest point at 17:49 BST on Saturday but it was later, when the sky got darker, that it made its biggest impact.

BBC Weather Watchers have been submitting the photos they took and here are a few of our favourites of those submitted so far.

News.title: ‘She could lose her life’: Husband of British mother-of-four detained on Egypt trip makes emotional plea to PM
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The husband of a British mother-of-four who has been detained in a maximum-security facility in Egypt for six weeks has urged the UK government to help secure her release.

Eman el-Shazly, 45, travelled to Cairo to visit her mother when she was taken by Egyptian security forces on 17 August, according to her husband Zeesharn Moustapha.

The property was “smashed up” and the family say they were told to tell her activist sister Mona to stop publishing criticism, before officers returned to take el-Shazly and another sister, Shaema, the following day.

Moustapha said that the last thing he heard was his wife saying: “They’re going to take me” before the line went dead.

Since that day, the family has had no contact with Eman and say that she has been refused a lawyer. They do not know the condition she is in and are concerned for her welfare.

The family believe that she is being detained over social media videos posted by her sister Mona that have been critical of the Egyptian government.

open image in gallery Eman el-Shazly is a 'strong-willed' person, her husband says ( Zesharn Moustapha )

Now he says his wife is facing a “kangaroo court” and fears for her safety. Last week the family launched a petition to “bring Eman home” and asked prime minster Andy Burnham and foreign secretary Ed Milband to use their influence to secure her release.

The couple share four children including three sons aged 18, 16 and nine and a 14-year-old daughter.

Moustapha says that the children have been forced to start the new school year without their mother and that they have been left “traumatised” by the ordeal.

“They’ve been upset, distraught, crying,” he told The Independent. “It was my son’s 10th birthday and he’s saying, ‘Mummy’s going to miss my birthday.’ It’s an emotional time for a young boy.”

The family have seen Eman’s brothers arrested on “identical” charges, with Moustapha saying that the men were previously held in pre-trial detention for around three years, before the charges were dropped and they were re-arrested in May this year.

They were accused of “promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation on social media, as well as broadcasting false news harmful to state security”.

Due to the previous cases, Moustapha says that his children are worried that the situation will be repeated for their mother.

open image in gallery The couple have four children and fear for the missing mother’s safety ( Zesharn Moustapha )

“She’s quite a strong-willed person but something like that would break anyone,” Moustapha says. “I’d be on the floor crying, you’re in a different country and then thrown into jail on fake charges.”

Moustapha has implored the prime minister to get involved in the case.

“We need the prime minister to get directly involved,” he said. “Make that call to Egypt and get this problem resolved because at the end of the day what they’re doing is against all human rights.

“There’s no legal basis for any of them to be arrested and it’s just an act of collective punishment. And now, there’s a British citizen, a mouther-of-four, in a maximum security prison who is completely innocent.”

He says that one of the brothers has been ill and has been refused medical attention. He fears the worst could happen to his wife.

“If my wife gets sick there, she could lose her life there,” he says. “Is the life of a British citizen not important to him [Burnham]?”

Mona el-Shazly told The Independent that she refuses to stop speaking out despite the treatment of her siblings and the fact that four families have been affected.

“Because yielding to intimidation means allowing fear to dictate who is permitted to speak. I understand completely why anyone under this level of pressure would want the nightmare to end, and I am terrified for my family's safety every single day,” she said.

“But stopping would establish a dangerous precedent: that an authoritarian regime can silence criticism anywhere in the world simply by taking family members hostage.

“I have zero tolerance for coercion. I have a duty to speak truthfully about corruption and abuse. My family must be released unconditionally because they are innocent individuals, not bargaining chips to control my voice.”

open image in gallery The family has appeared directly to prime minister Andy Burnham for help ( AFP/Getty )

Ayoub Khan, MP for Birmingham Perry Barr, told The Independent that the local community had been left “distraught by the continued detention”, which means Eman has “now been separated from her loved ones for two months.”

“No one deserves to lose their freedom as punishment for someone else speaking out lawfully against injustice,” he said.

“I will keep working with Eman’s legal representatives – and pressing the British and Egyptian Governments – to secure Eman’s immediate release and return to her family.”

Arfan Rashid, a lawyer representing Moustapha, told The Independent: “The FCDO informed us on 15 September that the Egyptian authorities accuse Eman of joining and financing a terrorist organisation, using social media accounts to spread false news, and calling citizens to demonstrate and gather. Eman denies wrongdoing.

“Her Egyptian lawyer tells us that he has been provided with no evidence supporting those allegations. We therefore cannot assess what, if anything, the authorities say Eman herself did to justify her continued detention.

“The family has serious reasons to question whether the case is connected to her sister Mona’s criticism of the Egyptian government.”

A British government report released in March 2026 referenced the “targeting, arrest and harassment of family members of government critics, journalists, and human rights activists living abroad”.

The FCDO told The Independent: “We are supporting the family of a British national detained in Egypt and are in contact with the authorities.”

The Independent has contacted the Egyptian embassy and No 10 for comment.

News.title: Ranulph Fiennes’ stepson claims police have ignored him in search for explorer
News.content:

Sir Ranulph Fiennes’s stepson has claimed that police are ignoring him over his pleas for help to find the missing explorer.

Alexander Millington-Cotes is urging an investigation into his 82-year-old stepfather’s whereabouts amid serious concerns over the conditions of his care.

It comes after a care home owner in Wales, where Sir Ranulph had been placed for seven weeks this year, told The Telegraph they had reported several issues about his wellbeing to the authorities.

Mr Millington-Cotes has said hehas been unable to see his stepfather for more than a year and has had “no luck” in hearing back from police.

He told The Telegraph: “It’s a real challenge because I don’t think anyone quite knows where he is. I’m trying to establish from the police what they’re doing… I’ve tried to get in touch but no luck so far.”

open image in gallery A GoFundMe page has been set up to help locate Sir Ranulph ( Getty )

He said he contacted several police forces in the locations where he believes his father might be, including Cheshire Constabulary, as Sir Ranulph had been moved to a facility there this year.

Mr Millington-Cotes visited the care home in Cheshire last week and was told by staff his stepfather was not there.

He also asked for help from West Mercia Police, which covers Shropshire, where their family home is, but received no response.

The stepson is urging for action to be taken “swiftly” and has set up a GoFundMe page that has so far raised more than £6,500 so far.

He told the newspaper: “I haven’t been able to speak to him and have the opportunity to say, what would you like to do? Be it, having some care from home, somewhere familiar, or to go and live his days in the Caribbean?

“I just want to be able to see him, for him to be able to see who he wants to, go where he wants with any support that he might need. This just seems like a really bad dream.”

open image in gallery The Care Inspectorate of Wales reportedly said Sir Ranulph was being ‘unlawfully deprived of his liberty’

The Telegraph reported that Care Inspectorate of Wales had said in an email to the care home owner in Wales that Sir Ranulph was being “unlawfully deprived of his liberty”.

A spokesperson said: “Care Inspectorate Wales is committed to promoting the safety, wellbeing and rights of people who receive social care services across Wales.

“As part of this role, CIW monitors Deprivation of Liberty Safeguards (DoLS) to help ensure people living in care homes are protected and any restrictions placed on their freedom are lawful, necessary and in their best interests.

“Where a person is under continuous supervision and control, is not free to leave, and lacks the capacity to consent to their care arrangements, providers must apply to the local authority for a DoLS authorisation and notify CIW when an application has been made.

“It would not be appropriate for us to comment on an individual's personal circumstances or care arrangements.”

The Independent approached West Mercia and Cheshire police forces for comment Saturday evening but have had no response.

News.title: Pandas depart China en route to Atlanta’s zoo for 10-year stay
News.content:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

A pair of giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, departed from Chengdu, China, on Sunday morning to begin a 10-year stay at Zoo Atlanta as part of a joint agreement between the Chinese and American governments.

Chinese President Xi Jinping announced the arrival of the pandas during a summit in Washington with US President Donald Trump, framing the agreement as a demonstration of diplomatic goodwill.

The temporary panda transfer stands as one of the few concrete outcomes from the state visit between President Trump and President Xi, which highlighted public displays of unity without resolving deeper diplomatic disagreements.

Both born in 2020 at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, the pandas will re-establish Zoo Atlanta's exhibit following the departure of its previous pandas in 2024.

Separately, Donald Trump met with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York to discuss key international matters including trade, energy, and immigration.

News.content:

Maybe it was just a coincidence. Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly gave the ball, and as a result goals, away. Rodri flew into a rash, and uncharacteristic, challenge and conceded a penalty, if not a goal when Harry Kane struck the bar. The common denominator, besides the fact each happened in Spain’s 3-2 win over England, is that they were Manchester City teammates last season. Thomas Tuchel denied his two defenders were distracted by the events of the previous day. It would be understandable if they were.

Rodri, too. For City alumni like him, there are legacies on the line. For the current squad, there are rather greater implications from the revelations the club has been found guilty of 114 of the charges the Premier League levelled. If so, City are highly likely to appeal. They are conscious at the Etihad Stadium that Uefa gave them a two-year Champions League ban in 2020 and it was later overturned. None of which guarantees a repeat and a reprieve now. With punishments potentially including huge points penalties and, directly or indirectly, ending up out of the Premier League, there might be an existential threat, even before factoring in the chance other clubs could take legal action against City which could radically reshape their finances.

All of which leaves players in limbo when, for many, their future had seemed secure. City have spent almost £500m on new signings in 2026, even before factoring in the considerable cost of contracts. But players had committed to them, too. Neither appeared paralysed by a sense of peril about what could transpire.

Guehi and Antoine Semenyo signed in January. Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez, Ayyoub Bouaddi, Jeremy Monga, Iliman Ndiaye, Allan Elias and Geronimo Rulli followed in the summer. There was also a raft of long-term contracts: for Phil Foden, Jeremy Doku, Josko Gvardiol and Abdukodir Khusanov. Before then, Rico Lewis and O’Reilly signed five-year deals last September. Then there is a new manager, in Enzo Maresca, who was so eager to join City that he ended up having to pay £17m in compensation to Chelsea.

None came with a guarantee of trophies but, presumably, each arrived or extended his stay with an assumption that City would remain a force, a club likely to be in the Champions League every year and which could attract and retain high-quality players. Now, with everything up in the air, such certainties can appear destroyed.

open image in gallery Lamine Yamal of Spain takes on Marc Guehi of England ( Getty )

Players and coaches may not elicit much sympathy, and not merely because of their pay packets. But if they were lured into a false sense of security, it may be in part because City have done a good job of acting as though it was business as usual; and for three-and-a-half years, it was. Perhaps players, like many in the fanbase, believed the club had “irrefutable evidence” of their position, as chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak put it on Saturday; perhaps they were reassured by his statement then. For years, Pep Guardiola was the most vehement in City’s defence. That might have given the dressing room confidence.

It does feel notable, though, that since City were charged in 2023, there is no evidence any player has left or declined to join because of the possible consequences of a guilty verdict. While Rodri and Bernardo Silva moved in on the summer, if they had been frightened about the independent panel’s ruling, they could have tried to engineer an exit sooner. When Kevin De Bruyne left, he had hoped to stay. Guardiola had extended his own contract during the years when the charges cast a shadow. So, most dramatically, did Erling Haaland, who has almost eight seasons left on the nine-and-a-half year deal he signed in January 2025.

open image in gallery Nico O'Reilly of England holds off Lamine Yamal of Spain ( Getty )

Figures of such stature have options. It is apparent, too, that City have bought players who had admirers at clubs who were not facing a century of charges: Guehi had almost joined Liverpool last August, Semenyo was liked by Liverpool, Tottenham and Manchester United, Anderson was wanted at Old Trafford, Arsenal were apparently interested in Bouaddi, Spurs bid for Ndiaye. In each case, it now looks as though the footballer overlooked the worst-case scenario when making his choice.

Footballing logic dictates that, if City had to have a fire sale, most would get takers, and probably at a high level. But that is an opinion, not a promise; for now, each may be staring into an abyss.

open image in gallery Erling Haaland has eight years left on his Man City contract ( Getty )

One of the unanswered, but intriguing, questions about City’s recent history is what their most intelligent footballers – men such as Silva, De Bruyne, Rodri, Ruben Dias, Manuel Akanji and Ilkay Gundogan – had felt about the charges and the possible personal implications; were they privy to private information that brought comfort?

Now, while Dias remains, while City’s achievements in the last 15 years may be reappraised, the chances are that no one is coming for Rodri’s medals, and not least because the most recent of the Premier League charges dated from 2018, before he joined. But there are more immediate issues for the newer generation, the 17 players who are contracted until the 2030s and who may now be studying the small print in search of release clauses. Suddenly, their futures seem very uncertain.

News.title: RAF Fairford: Five men arrested for ‘preparing a terrorist act’ near airbase used by US
