Five men detained near an RAF based used by the US have been arrested on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act.

A major incident has been declared and 85 homes have been evacuated near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after several men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences Sunday morning.

Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed it is leading the investigation into the incident footage from the scene showed a British Army bomb disposal squad using specialist robotic equipment to examine three white vans.

A force spokesperson said: “At around 12.45am today, police received a call relating to three suspicious vehicles which appeared to be travelling towards the air base.

“Armed officers responded and five men were arrested in the Whelford area on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act. They were further arrested on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act, contrary to section 5 of the Terrorism Act.”

open image in gallery Police at a road block near RAF Fairford (Ben Birchall/PA) ( PA Wire )

The base hosts the United States Air Force (USAF) and has been used to launch operations against Iran during the Middle East conflict.

In March this year, after then prime minister Sir Keir Starmer granted permission for “defensive” US action against Iranian missile sites from UK bases, four American bombers landed at RAF Fairford and the US started using British bases for “specific defensive operations”.

Fairford has been raised to the highest threat level, Delta, while US airbase Lakenheath in Suffolk is on Charlie alert, the second-highest threat level that can be issued by the US Department of Defence.

The police operation near the village of Whelford in Gloucestershire was not intelligence-led, meaning investigators had not known about any potential plot in advance.

Julian Tudsbery, who has lived in Whelford for 30 years, said a resident had reported three “suspicious vans” in the village in the early hours of Sunday morning.

“Evidently, they phoned the airbase police, who didn’t answer the phone,” he said. “It just rang out so she dialled 999.”

He said he was evacuated at around 7am, adding: “(The police) were then banging on the door, so I went downstairs in my dressing gown.

open image in gallery Counter terror police are leading the investigation ( PA )

“There were several police, three police cars in the drive, and they said you need to evacuate, there’s been a major incident, said he couldn’t elaborate.”

A 400m cordon has been put in place around the vehicles while villagers were evacuated to a nearby leisure centre.

A large emergency services presence was seen in the area, including a Hazardous Area Response Team, the fire service and local police.

Gloucestershire Police said: “A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident.

“It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act. The Army’s specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles.

“The local residents are being evacuated to a nearby leisure centre. A cordon is currently in place but we’d like to reassure people that we believe this incident is contained.

“We are working closely with our partners and are enacting the well-rehearsed plans we have in place.”

The circumstances around the current incident are not yet known. In July, the British government insisted it “stands ready 24/7 to defend itself” after Iran said UK airbases used by the US were considered “legitimate targets”.

open image in gallery A US Air Force B-1 Lancer bomber is pictured on the tarmac at RAF Fairford ( AFP/Getty )

Investigators will be working to analyse any devices seized from those arrested to establish details of any plot and any potential motivation.

A spokesperson for the US Air Force said its personnel based at RAF Fairford “remain vigilant”.

“For operational security reasons we will not discuss specific force protection measures,” the spokesperson added.

“The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families.

“We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families.”

Security measures at the site in southwest England have significantly increased with roadblocks and armed police preventing access and emergency vehicles parked nearby, Reuters reported on Sunday.

The airbase also hosts the annual Royal International Air Tattoo (RIAT), though this year’s event in May was cancelled because of the military operations.

open image in gallery Fire crews are at the scene after a major incident was declared in Fairford ( Reuters )

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, currently attending the annual Labour Party conference in Liverpool, is receiving updates on the situation.

A government spokesperson added: “We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe.

“It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting confirmed the incident is “being dealt with” and thanked the emergency teams who acted “so swiftly”.

“It is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24/7,” he added.

A woman living on the base’s perimeter described an apparent increase in military security in recent weeks.

open image in gallery RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk has also been put on high alert ( Reuters )

The woman, who asked not to be identified, told the Press Association: “In the prior few weeks they have put heavy, very heavy, vehicles across all gates.”

She described them as “very big tractors and things like that” parked behind crash-gates into the base, adding: “So obviously they’re taking security seriously”.

“Great big concrete walls” have also been placed behind some gates, including on Dunfield Loop and Whelford Road, the resident, who has lived there for about 50 years, told the press association.

The arrests come amid heightened concerns around the threat from hostile states to the UK, with Russia and Iran among those that have used proxies to commit crimes on their behalf on British soil.

More follows on this developing news story...

The future of Giorgio Armani ’s empire is coming into sharper focus a year after the designer’s death. On the runway in Milan, his signature elegance defined the latest collection previewed on Sunday, while behind the scenes talks are set to begin on the sale of a stake, as stipulated in his will.

Armani gave preference to LVMH, L’Oréal and EssilorLuxottica as potential buyers of a 15% stake to be sold within 18 months of his death on Sept. 4, 2025, at the age of 91.

Chief Executive Giuseppe Marsocci told reporters backstage at the runway show that there were no favorites and that the stake could potentially be split among all three companies.

“It is not written in stone that there has to be one,” he said.

Marsocci said the will allowed discussions to begin only after the first anniversary of Armani’s death but declined to confirm whether they had started. “The assumption” that talks were underway “may have some logic,” he said.

The recent appointment of Dario Vitale as head of accessories at Giorgio Armani and creative director of Emporio Armani has generated interest in the fashion house’s creative future. No date has been announced for his runway debut.

Asked whether Vitale’s role could expand, Marsocci said everything was evolving. “From here into the future, you never know,” he said.

The womenswear collection for next spring and summer deliberately mixed daywear with evening looks, with sparkle running through both. Lean, fluid trousers and long dresses shaped the silhouette, often paired with rigid bodices. The collection was titled “Evolution.”

“It evolved in the sense that it is fashion that everyone can wear,” said Silvana Armani, the late designer’s niece and longtime head of womenswear.

She departed from her uncle’s legacy in one important way: incorporating cotton, a textile that she said he didn’t like but which she “adores.”

The designer’s presence was most felt in the collection in two pieces: a recreation of the formal double-breasted Communion suit that Armani wore when he was 8-years-old and a graphic jacket bearing his smiling image.

A month on from Nepal’s devastating floods, the disaster looks set to pile billions of pounds onto the country’s national debt burden – as experts warn it could become the latest country to face a huge debt bill from a climate crisis it has done little to cause.

On 26 August, more than 100 million cubic metres of rock and glacier broke away from Langtang Lirung mountain on Nepal’s northern border, triggering a 188km/h debris flood that buried villages, changed the course of rivers, and killed more than 1,400 people.

Scientists have since said that the event was made significantly more likely due to climate change, while the finance minister has warned that the final death toll could exceed that of a devastating 2015 earthquake.

A subsequent rapid assessment of damage from the Nepalese government has put the cost of recovery and reconstruction at $4.8bn (£3.6bn) – equivalent to 11 per cent of the country’s GDP – and government figures have called for grant-based compensation as a matter of “climate justice”, given the fact that Nepal contributes to an estimated 0.1 per cent of greenhouse gas emissions each year.

open image in gallery Nepal suffered one of the worst catastrophes in its history when a tsunami-like flood cut a swathe of destruction claiming more than 1,400 lives and leaving 5,000 unaccounted for ( AFP/Getty )

But the Fund for responding to Loss and Damage, established at the UN climate summit COP27 in Egypt in 2022, has so far secured just $822m in pledges, of which only $456m has actually been paid in, limiting the scale of support available to countries hit by disasters.

The fact that applications for withdrawals are limited to only $20m per country means the government will likely be forced to foot the bill with public debt, according to experts.

“The loss and damage fund was created to support countries facing unprecedented climate disasters such as this, but it has nowhere near enough money,” says Ritu Bharadwaj, director of climate resilience at the International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED).

“Even if – by a stroke of luck – they received the $20m they can apply for, that is less than half of a percent of the $4.8bn in damages.”

Bharadwaj continues: “Right now, there is still media attention. But once that goes, Nepal will be left to fend for itself – and that will mean borrowing huge amounts of money at an expensive rate, leaving the country at the mercy of creditors who can essentially use debt to control the country in an almost colonial manner.”

open image in gallery People search for their belongings at a damaged house in Devighat, Nepal, this week ( Reuters )

Bharadwaj’s comments come as campaigners have for many months now warned that decisive global action must be taken to address soaring debt levels in developing countries. Low-income nations now spend an average of 18 per cent of government revenue servicing external debt, which these days is often held by private financial institutions, and countries are also paying billions more to cover debts than they are receiving as aid to fight climate crisis.

Nepal’s own national debt has risen sharply over the past seven years, from Rs 1.43 trillion in 2019/20 to nearly Rs 3 trillion (£7bn to £15bn). The Asian Development Bank has also warned that the August floods will likely weigh on Nepal’s GDP this year.

“Countries were like Nepal were not responsible for for polluting our planet,” said Sarah Champion, the Labour MP and chair of the International Development Committee. “We need to make sure that they are not left with insurmountable debt as a consequence of climate change disasters.”

If – as many fear – Nepal’s debt is sent soaring by the costs of recovering from the flooding disaster, it will be just the latest developing country to suffer in such a way from a climate disaster they bear little responsibility towards.

New analyses from Debt Justice, shared exclusively with The Independent, show how a pattern of pattern has already played out elsewhere.

In Mozambique, Cyclone Freddy caused an estimated $1.5bn in damage in 2023. By 2025, the country’s public debt had climbed to 91.4 per cent of GDP, $1.4bn higher than the IMF had predicted before the cyclone struck, which is a gap roughly equivalent to the disaster’s cost.

Mozambique’s debt was declared unsustainable by the IMF this February, after the country slipped into debt-service arrears estimated at 1.3 per cent of GDP in 2025.

A similar story played out after Pakistan’s 2010 floods, which caused an estimated $43bn in losses.

The IMF had forecast the country’s fiscal deficit would shrink steadily in the years that followed; instead it more than doubled, driving Pakistan to borrow an estimated $20bn-$40bn more than it otherwise would have. Debt Justice calculates that, once interest payments are factored in, the floods added $36bn to $71bn to the country’s debt burden over the following decade.

“Mozambique and Pakistan’s debt levels were much higher than originally predicted after the climate disasters,” says Tess Woolfenden, policy adviser at Debt Justice. “While not all increases can be put down to the disaster, the increase, alongside a well-known lack of grant-based climate finance, indicates the harmful impact these disasters have contributed to increases in government debt.”

She continues: “Rich countries that have built their wealth on climate-wrecking emissions cannot ignore the billions of dollars of damage now facing Nepal. They must urgently pay what they owe, as grants, not loans.”

The pattern is also extremely evident among the world’s 39 small-island developing states, which are now regularly being thrown into chaos by climate disasters, such as Hurricane Melissa in Jamaica last year.

More than 40 per cent of these countries are currently classified as highly indebted or in “debt distress” – and analysis from IIED’s Bharadwaj finds that the mean external debt of island states increased from 55 per cent during a period of low disaster intensity (2007-09) to 59 per cent during a period of high disaster intensity (2020-21).

The nature of the escalating climate crisis means that climate disasters are now often hitting before a country has had time to recover from a previous such event.

“If you look back just one year, Nepal faced a similar big flooding event, and some of the roads were still being rebuilt when this latest flood occurred,” says Bharadwaj. “For countries like Nepal there is no recourse, as they are battered by the weather and the global financial system.”

NGOs who are either helping to fund the humanitarian response, or actively developing programmes to assist, share similar views that wealthy nations must urgently step up support for Nepal in the wake of its latest disaster.

“A country suffering a natural disaster should have an immediate, interest-free suspension of all debt payments across all external creditors as an act of solidarity and a recognition of the long-term impacts suffered,” says Neil Thorns, director of advocacy at CAFOD.

“Recovery should not leave countries like Nepal taking on any additional unaffordable or inappropriate debt to pay for disasters they did little to cause,” agrees Shruti Agarwal, senior climate finance adviser at Save the Children. “It is critical that climate finance remains affordable for lower-income countries and is grounded in the principles of climate justice.”

As well as calling for more grant-based support, campaigners argue that rich countries can do much more to assist developing countries struggling under excessive debt burdens.

This could include reforming the existing G20 debt relief process – known as the Common Framework – to compel creditors to better engage with the process, or via UK legislation that capitalises on the fact that some 90 per cent of developing country debt eligible for debt relief is legally domiciled in the UK, as a result of the strength of the City of London.

“Rich countries need to urgently agree on a mechanism to cancel unjust debts, including to private lenders,” says Woolfenden. “The UK should use its presidency of the G20 next year to radically reform the current debt relief mechanism.”

This article has been produced as part of The Independent’s Rethinking Global Aid project

The East Coast is bracing for more rain Sunday as a deadly nor’easter storm continues to wreak havoc on the region for a third day.

Hazardous conditions spread across the U.S. Northeast on Saturday as the formidable, slow-moving storm lashed the coastline with intense gales, torrential rainfall, and rough surf that knocked out power across the region.

A municipal worker for the New York City Housing Authority was killed in Brooklyn when a tree collapsed amid fierce gusts and heavy downpours. Across New England and the mid-Atlantic, emergency personnel worked to clear fallen timber and restore electricity after blackouts affected approximately 100,000 households and businesses.

Tens of millions of residents throughout the region remained under severe weather threats into Sunday, with significant coastal inundation expected. The Federal Emergency Management Agency confirmed that regional response coordination hubs were operating at an "enhanced posture," while specialized assistance teams were on standby in New England to manage potential widespread utility failures.

open image in gallery Waves pound the coast as the tide comes in during a Nor'Easter storm in Scituate, Massachusetts on September 26, 2026 ( AFP via Getty Images )

Meteorologists warned that conditions would not improve immediately. There will be "a lot of high winds, a lot of high tides and heavy rain possibility over the next few days for the northeastern U.S.," said Bob Oravec, lead forecaster with the National Weather Service in College Park, Maryland.

Peak tidal surges were expected to hit shorelines north of Atlantic City, New Jersey, from Saturday evening into Sunday, threatening widespread inundation of roadways in bayfront and coastal neighborhoods, the National Weather Service said.

"Anyone who goes in or near the water this weekend is literally gambling with their life," New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said.

Residents in parts of New York and New Jersey navigated submerged roads by kayak, while adventurous surfers targeted unusually large ocean swells. In Sea Bright, New Jersey, first responders extracted a woman and her dog after their vehicle became trapped in floodwaters, ABC7 reported.

Rising waters submerge roads and businesses

Inside the coastal New Jersey borough of Surf City, Kenny Formica monitored security cameras from his home, watching floodwaters seep into the marina he owns. Water breaching the building is an exceptional event, Formica explained, noting the last occurrence was during Hurricane Sandy in 2012, which he said caused more than $4 million in damage to his business.

Prior to the storm's arrival, marina staff fastened dock lines, relocated loose gear out of harm’s way, and staged company trucks and forklifts on the highest ground available.

Upon waking, Formica found messages from boat owners reporting displaced vessels and watercraft. A customer forwarded video footage captured around 4 a.m. showing his 25-foot (7.6-meter) boat after it had blown off its lift.

open image in gallery A family carries their belongings through the water of a flooded road during a nor'easter storm on September 26, 2026 in Point Pleasant, New Jersey ( Getty Images )

Farther south, in Norfolk, Virginia, Ellie Hodge observed from her front porch as driving traffic generated wakes along flooded streets. The coastal city saw isolated flooding all week because of the nor’easter.

"We've seen cars get stuck on the road, going up the sidewalks," Hodge said. "It's been pretty bad this time around."

Travel disruptions and canceled events

Travel itineraries across the region were upended. Hundreds of flights were canceled at Boston Logan International Airport, as were the vast majority of flights at the popular Massachusetts tourist destinations of Martha's Vineyard and Nantucket.

Along the North Carolina coast, a flooding-related highway closure on Hatteras Island disrupted Jayden Sink and Kimberly Laprad’s wedding plans. The Virginia couple made it onto the island before the storm, but most of their roughly 45 guests were stranded on the other side of the closure, the Island Free Press reported. A local campground offered a new venue, cabins and an officiant, and a DJ volunteered to provide music.

With the primary roadway shut down and local ferry service also out of service, boat travel through bad weather remained the only option, said Drew Pearson, emergency management director for North Carolina’s Dare County. The island has a year-round population of about 5,000 that swells much higher in warm weather, he said.

The North Carolina Department of Transportation said it would soon begin emergency ferry service between Hatteras Island and the mainland.

"To folks on Hatteras, you are not on an island all alone," Gov. Josh Stein said on social media. "North Carolina and county emergency responders are working hard to keep you safe and reconnected as quickly as possible."

Authorities urge vigilance

Nor’easters are not unusual as New England moves into the fall season, but "this might be a little earlier than average for a big storm," said Oravec, of the National Weather Service.

The storm’s slow movement could worsen beach erosion by subjecting the coast to a prolonged period of strong winds and waves, he said.

Hochul said coastal flooding was the biggest threat, but heavy rains, powerful winds and waves as high as 20 feet (6 meters) were also expected.

On Long Island, ferry owner Stephanie Sherman paused operations between Patchogue and the barrier island of Fire Island.

"It’s been a pretty wild storm," Sherman said. "But nothing that we haven’t experienced in the past. These happen every so often."

News.title: Australia hold on to beat Boks in Test match for the ages after being reduced to 11 players
News.content:
Australia 42 South Africa 38

If the Wallabies play like this in their own back yard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the two-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Joseph Suaalii were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

Boss Marco Rossi added on the incident: “I didn’t see what happened at the end of the game.

“There may have been some insults towards Dominik, and our players may have taken up the gloves, but I really don’t know exactly why the guys got so pumped up.

“We didn’t deserve to lose, but we lost, that’s football. We missed every chance, they took advantage of their first goal opportunity.”

Hungary will be back in action on Monday night when they take on Northern Ireland in Belfast.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes cut from Portugal squad due to UEFA rules and 'complicated' issue
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes cut from Portugal squad due to UEFA rules and 'complicated' issue

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been dealing with an injury issue and will not be included in Portugal's squad to face Norway in Oslo on Sunday night

View 3 Images Manchester United and Portugal midfielder Bruno Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes has been left out of Portugal’s squad to face Norway on Sunday night.

‌



The Manchester United skipper came off in the final minutes of the win over Wales in Lisbon. Portugal boss Jorge Jesus then admitted Fernandes was struggling with a ‘complicated’ problem he has played through for the Red Devils.

‌



He was then absent from training on Saturday, with his name omitted from the official UEFA lists published on the day of the game. UEFA rules stipulate that a maximum of 23 players can be named in a matchday squad, with Goncalo Inacio drafted in after missing the game vs Wales.

‌



Jesus had already suggested the United star would miss the trip to Oslo, in order for him to potentially be available against Denmark on Thursday.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He said: “In the game against Wales, we went in with all the available players but Bruno Fernandes came off with a complicated problem.

“We’ll see what happens until tomorrow. Experience tells me that on the third day not all players manage to recover but that’s the same for Norway as for us. However, the player who comes in gives as many guarantees as the one who might come off, that’s what I’ll base my decision on.”

Jesus added: “The medical team identified these two players as the most concerning, Nuno Mendes could be available for the game.

‌



View 3 Images Jorge Jesus gave an update on Fernandes' fitness (Image: Patricia de Melo Moreira / AFP via Getty Images)

“The other case [Fernandes] involves treatment and recovery time. He’s coming off an injury at United, and he told me he’s been playing with that pain for the last three games, which is hindering him.

“It was one of the factors that prevented Bruno from playing at his best against Wales. I’ve already spoken to him and I prefer not to risk it in this game so he’s fully fit for the Denmark match.”

‌



After scoring a hat-trick in the win over Ipswich at the end of August, Fernandes has gone three Premier League matches without registering a goal or an assist. He played 90 minutes against Man City and Fulham in the week leading up to the break, with United picking up a point from the two games.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has hinted Fernandes will be rotated this season to preserve fitness (Image: ANDY BUCHANAN/AFP via Getty Images)

United boss Michael Carrick has already suggested he will attempt to rotate Fernandes in and out of the side in the coming months, with the added fixtures in the Champions League.

Article continues below

Carrick said: “In terms of the games and how it comes, hopefully he stays fit and he’s in good shape. But yeah, there’s the element talking about the squad and the depth, and as we go through the season and the waves and the momentum and keeping the boys in good form, but keeping them fresh as well.

“So Bruno’s part of that. He’s a big player for us, he’s obviously our captain, but there’s still elements where we need to look after him.”

Sports.title: Spanish media react exactly as expected to Antony Gordon display as England team-mate ridiculed
Sports.content:
Spanish media react exactly as expected to Antony Gordon display as England team-mate ridiculed

Anthony Gordon's performance against Spain earned plenty of attention in the Spanish media as the Barcelona star impressed at Wembley - but one team-mate in particular wasn't so lucky

View 2 Images Anthony Gordon left his mark on the Spanish media despite England's UEFA Nations League loss at Wembley (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

England's 3-2 defeat by Spain in their UEFA Nations League opener saw Anthony Gordon come away with his reputation intact. The Barcelona winger's incisive finish pulled the Three Lions level at Wembley, only to fall victim to a second-half collapse.

‌



Thomas Tuchel's side started on the back foot after conceding almost immediately to a predatory Lamine Yamal finish. Gordon's Barca team-mate pilfered Marc Guehi deep in his own half before finishing smartly past James Trafford.

‌



It was a night of mixed messages for England, who showed fight to lead at half-time thanks to Harry Kane's go-ahead goal. And Gordon received the glut of positive plaudits in the Spanish media despite a tough night for the Wembley hosts.

‌



Assessing the performance of Spain right-back Marc Pubill, AS said: "At times, it was clear he's more accustomed to playing center-back than full-back, and he was outplayed by Barcelona's Gordon, the star of the night at Wembley."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The same newspaper counted Gordon as one of five England players to receive a two-out-of-three rating. Jude Bellingham, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Elliot Anderson and Bukayo Saka were the only others to match that mark.

‌



England come out on wrong side of Spain thriller but Thomas Tuchel gets fans back onside READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel brutally shuts down England question live on ITV with blunt answer READ MORE :

Marca saw it almost identically, except Harry Kane was also counted as a sixth player to receive that commendation. The same couldn't be said for Guehi, who was lambasted following his role in Yamal's breakthrough.

"The paranormal events include Spain's first goal after a joke by Guehi," read its assessment of the opening goal. The same match review described the Manchester City defender's 'howler' before giving him the lowest grade possible.

View 2 Images Marc Guehi's early mistake allowed Lamine Yamal in to score after less than two minutes (Image: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



Marca ranks players on a one-to-three-star basis, with scorers Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarazabal the only players to receive the highest grades. Guehi, on the other hand, was the only player on the field to receive a zero-star grade following his early slip in front of goal.

AS also piled in on Guehi's misery by deriding his contribution leading up to Yamal's 104-second opener. The Barcelona ace capitalised on the England defender's sluggish start and 'pickpocketed' his opposite man in cunning fashion.

"He pulled out the football book he used to teach in the parks of Mataró and, like the street smarts he always was, anticipated Guehi's next move, snatched his wallet, and positioned himself in front of the centre-back to show him that either he let him finish the play, or he'd be sent off," read its review.

‌

Guehi was guilty of endangering himself and the team with his dithering in defence, which put the ball on a plate for Yamal. The City man got more into the match over time, though that early gaffe inevitably left a significant stain on his display.

All in all, England shouldn't rake themselves over the coals too much for what was an embattled display against the current world champions. And after previously being slated by sections of the Spanish media for his displays at Barca, Gordon is steadily improving his reputation in the country he now calls home.

Sports.title: Man City relegation could 'lead to legal disputes' with stars as 115 charges punishment wait begins
Sports.content:
Man City relegation could 'lead to legal disputes' with stars as 115 charges punishment wait begins

Manchester City may be facing questions from their own players and their respective futures over the club being found in breach of financial regulations

View 2 Images Manchester City players could have a legal case to terminate their contracts if the club is relegated (Image: (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images))

Manchester City players have been told they could have a legal case for tearing up their contracts but that more consequences than just relegation may be required. The club have been found in breach of financial rules 114 times, though it is understood they will be appealing the decision.

‌



Multiple punishment verdicts have been issued since the news broke with a sizeable points deduction that causes relegation a possibility. However, any sanctions being imposed - alongside City's potential legal dispute with players and their contracts - will have to wait until the process is fully complete.

‌



That could take several years, particularly given City's likely plans to appeal each individual charge. Legal action from other Premier League clubs has also been mooted with that being just another scenario that follows the appeal.

‌



Erling Haaland U-turn confirmed immediately after Man City found guilty of 114 charges READ MORE :

Roy Keane and Ian Wright urge Premier League to punish Man City after 'cheat' verdict READ MORE :

City may also have to answer to their own players, particularly if they are relegated as a result of the punishment dished out in a hearing, However, it has been revealed they may need to prove that the club's alleged conduct impacted their choice to either sign for or remain at City.

Via The Sunday Times, Kavan Bakhda, a partner and the head of sports at Mishcon de Reya, said: “Relegation would not give Manchester City ’s players an automatic legal right to tear up their contracts and walk away. However, relegation could lead to thorny legal disputes between players and the club.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



"If Manchester City were relegated because of serious wrongdoing by the club, players could in theory argue that the club’s conduct amounted to a fundamental breach entitling them to terminate their contracts.

"However, these would be relatively high legal thresholds for players to reach. Relegation alone would not necessarily be enough."

View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak penned a message to worried Man City supporters on Saturday afternoon

‌



Despite the guilty verdict, City have protested their innocence since first being charged by the Premier League in February 2023. That stance was reiterated by club chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in a statement on Saturday as he stated that process has a long way to go.

Part of his comments, published on the club website, read: "I have been part of this Club for 18 years. I have had the privilege to stand with you in the Etihad, at Wembley, and in Istanbul. This Club matters to me, and you have shown and told me – time and time again - how much Manchester City matters to you. This is why I am writing to you today.

"Following Friday’s media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues. So have I. Here’s what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.

Article continues below

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies."

Sports.title: Brazil football legend 'lost 99%' of career earnings as warning sent to young players
Sports.content:
Brazil football legend 'lost 99%' of career earnings as warning sent to young players

The former left-back has opened up about 'mistakes' he made, which had big financial consequences

View 2 Images Roberto Carlos has claimed that he lost 99% of his career earnings. (Image: Clive Rose/Getty Images)

Legendary Brazilian left-back Roberto Carlos has revealed that he lost ‘99%’ of the earnings he made throughout his career. The former Real Madrid defender is estimated to have earned around €160 million (£137.6m) throughout his playing career.

‌



He is known as one of the best ever in his position, helping Brazil to win the World Cup in 2002. He also lifted the Champions League trophy three times with Real Madrid.

‌



Despite success on the pitch, the 53-year-old has admitted to ‘mistakes’ off it, which led to him losing a lot of money. He says it’s a warning for younger players.

‌



Thomas Tuchel brutally shuts down England question live on ITV with blunt answer READ MORE :

Manchester City apology demanded after Premier League charges verdict READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Speaking at the Portugal Football Summit, Carlos said: “I had problems with people who emptied my bank account. I lost 99% of everything I earned from football.”

He added: "I had a very serious family problem. On Thursday, I went to bed at midnight and on Friday, I received a pile of documents I knew nothing about. That’s when I realised I had lost my entire history.

‌



“I made mistakes, and therefore, I ask younger players not to do the same. I always thought about future plans after my playing career.

“It’s about building a history as a player and leveraging your image. When I decided to leave football, I already had my sporting director’s licence and was working with many brands.”

Carlos played 817 games for seven different clubs throughout a 20-plus-year career. He appeared to retire in 2012, but made a comeback in 2015, signing for Indian side Delhi Dynamos.

‌



View 2 Images Brazil legend Roberto Carlos during a legends match in 2022 (Image: Martin Rickett/PA Wire.)

He made just three appearances in the Indian Super League before announcing his retirement in 2016. He now works as a club representative for Real Madrid and is the owner of Brazilian third-tier side AA Internacional de Limeira, and was over in America for the summer's World Cup.

The former left-back underwent planned surgery last year, and moved to confirm that he did not suffer a heart attack. "I would like to clarify recent information that has been circling. I recently underwent a preventative medical procedure, planned in advance with my medical team," he wrote on Instagram.

Article continues below

"The procedure was successful, and I am well. I did not suffer a heart attack. I am recovering well, and looking forward to returning to full fitness and resuming my professional and personal commitments soon.

"I sincerely thank everyone for messages of support, care, and concern."

Sports.title: 11 footballers pick their Ballon d'Or winner as clear picture emerges of winner
Sports.content:
11 footballers pick their Ballon d'Or winner as clear picture emerges of winner

The winner of the 2026 Ballon d'Or will be announced in October with several big names nominated for the award

View 5 Images Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal share the lead in the Ballon d'Or race (Image: FRANCK FIFE/AFP via Getty Images)

Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal are leading the race for the Ballon d'Or this year, according to both the odds and their team-mates. The annual awards ceremony is coming up in October and there are several names in contention for the prize.

‌



Yamal and Kane are the hot favourites, followed by the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Ballon d'Or winners are judged on three specific criteria - individual performances, collective performances and titles won, plus class and fair play - although given the number of attackers that have won the award, unofficially it's clear that goals and assists weigh heavily, too.

‌



Last season, Yamal won the La Liga title and Supercopa trophy and reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League. He also completed international football by lifting the World Cup at just 19 years old, after winning the European Championships two years earlier with Spain.

‌



On the other hand, Kane won every domestic trophy available with Bayern while scoring a whopping 61 goals. He captained England to the semi-finals of the World Cup and scored five during the tournament.

There are plenty of arguments over who should win the Ballon d'Or, with some current players weighing in on who they think deserves it the most. Here, Mirror Football has revealed what the game's top stars think about who should walk away with the trophy.

Raphinha - Lamine Yamal

According to his Barcelona teammate Raphinha, there's no question that Yamal should receive the prestigious honour this year. He said: "I have no doubts. Lamine Yamal should win the Ballon d'Or.

‌



View 5 Images Raphinha has backed his Barca teammate to win the award (Image: Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

"It depends on individual stats, collective titles, magic, charisma, and many things. Lamine has them all. He has incredible numbers, and not only last season. Three titles, with a World Cup."

Lautaro Martinez - Lionel Messi

Lionel Messi is still receiving plaudits for his exceptional talent despite narrowly missing out on the World Cup. His Argentina teammate Lautaro Martinez believes the 39-year-old is still the greatest player in the world.

‌



"Who will win the Ballon d’Or? Messi. Without doubt,” the Inter Milan striker told TNT Brasil. "He is the best in the world. He is the best in the history of this sport. As long as he is on the pitch, he will have a chance."

Declan Rice - Harry Kane

View 5 Images Rice believes his England captain should win the award, despite being nominated himself (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

Declan Rice has been nominated for the award thanks to his key role in Arsenal's Premier League win and run to the Champions League final. However, the midfielder has backed his England captain to secure the Ballon d'Or as he said: "It’s the second year in a row I have been nominated.

‌



"It’s obviously really good. I’m really proud. Obviously I know who I want to win it. I’d love to see Harry Kane win it, so I’m wishing him all the best in that."

Michael Olise - Harry Kane

Bayern Munich won the domestic treble in Germany and made the Champions League semi-finals last season with the help of Michael Olise. He was a key part of this winning team but is adamant Kane should win the Ballon d'Or as he "was the best player last season."

Book England Nations League VIP tickets at Seat Unique This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more Various prices Seat Unique Book tickets here Product Description England fans can book tickets for each UEFA Nations League fixture at Wembley Stadium.

‌



Luis Diaz - Harry Kane

Fellow Bayern teammate Luis Diaz is in agreement with Olise, going more into depth as to why Kane deserves the personal honour. He said: "He does everything. [He] attacks, defends, assists. He was one of the top scorers in the whole world last season.

"That's why I think he deserves it. 100%. He always wants more, refuses to settle, and he helps you as a teammate to grow."

Lamine Yamal - Himself

Yamal has backed himself to win the award after scooping the Kopa Trophy for two consecutive years. The Barcelona talent named Mbappe as the other deserving nominee but believes he deserves it more.

‌



Speaking to Movistar+, the 19-year-old explained: "Who would I give it to? The best in the world. Who are they going to give it to? That’s a very long discussion.

"I honestly think that maybe there are two of us who are the best in the world. And I think I deserve it this year because of what I’ve won. Because for me, Mbappé and I are the two best in the world. For me, it’s very clear, and everyone who watches the games knows it."

Kylian Mbappe - Himself

Mbappe also believes he can secure the Ballon d'Or for his performances with Real Madrid and France last season. In an interview with France Football, the forward said: "I believe I can win it this year.

‌



"It’s one of my objectives, and a short-term one at that."

Rodri - Lamine Yamal

View 5 Images Plenty of people believe the teenager should collect the trophyv (Image: Gongora/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Summer signing Rodri believes his Barca teammate should win the Ballon d'Or and claimed that the award should definitely go to a Spain international. He told Mundo Deportivo: "What does the Ballon d'Or measure? Individual performance, the season?

‌



"We’re all drawn to individual titles, but I think that a 19-year-old who has been able to win what Lamine has won is impressive; it already speaks to his stature as a player. From there, we’ll see what they decide.

"I think it’s a very open year, where perhaps all the players on the shortlist have the merit to win it. So it’s not something that worries me too much. I would like a Spaniard to win it, whether it’s Lamine, Pau (Cubarsí), Fabián (Ruiz), or even me, whoever is nominated."

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia - Ousmane Dembele

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia won the Champions League with Paris Saint-Germain last year, making it back-to-back European titles for the Georgian star. Despite being nominated himself, Kvaratskhelia backed PSG teammate Ousmane Dembele to win the Ballon d'Or for the second year in a row.

‌



Kvaratskhelia told Ligue 1 Plus: " I think that, if I could vote, I would vote for Ousmane. He was there to support us and help the team. We understand each other very well, even off the pitch. It is very easy to understand how he plays football."

Ousmane Dembele - Khvicha Kvaratskhelia

Dembele has returned the favour to his PSG teammate by supporting Kvaratskhelia to win the award. He said: "I hope that a Parisien will win the Ballon d’Or and especially Kvara, who had an incredible season with PSG. He made a difference in all of the big matches. He had a great season. We hope that it will be either me or him."

The current Ballon d'Or holder added: "Off the pitch, we get on really well and on it, it is easy with a player of this quality. I already knew him before Napoli because I played Football Manager, so I knew him when he was at Rubin Kazan. He is an incredible player. We saw him at Napoli and now here at PSG. He has been with us for a year and a half, doing incredible things. Our complicity is natural."

‌



Sir David Beckham - Lionel Messi

View 5 Images Lionel Messi could break another record in football this year (Image: JC Ruiz/Getty Images)

And finally, former Premier League hero Sir David Beckham believes Messi should break another record by lifting his ninth Ballon d'Or award this year. Speaking after Inter Miami's Campeones Cup win, the ex-Manchester United man told Major League Soccer: "I still can't believe we have him in Miami playing for our team.

"That's why I go to training every day and watch him and turn up to watch him every time possible, because we want to see Leo play football forever. When you see him do things like tonight, and you see him have the World Cup he's had, it's not luck that he's being considered for the Ballon d'Or again.

Article continues below

"It's not luck. He was probably the best player in the tournament; he had an incredible year last year. At 39 years old, to affect the World Cup in every game the way he did, that's special. There's no one at 39 who is doing this at that level.

"He deserves to be considered for the Ballon d'Or. In my opinion, he should win it. You have great players in there, like Harry Kane, Kylian [Mbappe] and Jude Bellingham, and other players. But when talking about Leo, I'm his biggest supporter."

Sports.title: Why Tuchel's critics have been forced to stay quiet despite Spain loss
Sports.content:
The narrative before this first post-World Cup international was clear: if England lose, the pressure on Thomas Tuchel could become unbearable.

The big name on the big bucks, brought in to win the big games, could not afford to lose to Spain after the tactical disaster of the World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina. The court of public opinion, and the bile of the English media, would combine to make life very difficult for the England boss.

Well, here we are, in the aftermath of a 3-2 loss to the newly-crowned world champions, where England were outclassed on numerous occasions, where the scoreline should have been much one-sided, where for long periods Spain looked far superior to the Three Lions, where after half an hour the visitors should have been four-nil up. That's surely it, then? Auf Wiedersehen, Thomas?

Nope. Strangely, despite all of that, Tuchel's critics have been forced to bite their tongues and bide their time. Why? Because England were true to their DNA, they gave it a real good go; there were a lot of positive signs, and ultimately everyone saw again just how incredibly good Spain are.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Dorsett gives his verdict on England's 3-2 defeat to world champions Spain at Wembley in the Nations League

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett and Peter Smith rate the England players' performances in their Nations League loss against Spain

It's hard to criticise Tuchel or his players when they were narrowly beaten by a team who have repeatedly proven they are the best by a mile at what they do.

The game was decided by two collector's items at either end of the pitch - one a Marc Guehi calamity on the edge of his own box that gifted Spain the lead in the second minute. The other was a Harry Kane missed penalty because of a slippery pitch. And if England's captain had scored from 12 yards, giving his side a two-goal cushion, who knows what might have been.

The match statistics make for comforting reading for Tuchel too. Up against the tika-taka maestros, England had a very respectable 48 per cent possession, made more successful passes in the final third than Spain, had two fewer shots, had over double the amount of touches in the opponent's box and five times as many crosses.

Those stats may not pass the sniff test. They might seem at odds with what most spectators saw with their eyes, but the numbers that perhaps help us understand better show that Spain created twice as many big chances.

How do we digest all of that? In basic terms, Spain may have had the ball less than England in dangerous areas, but when they did, Luis de la Fuente's team had more quality and were more clinical. And the team that has not lost a match in two-and-a-half years didn't make costly individual errors with the ball, because that's not in their DNA.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Anthony Gordon reflects on defeat to Spain

If it is possible, the defeat has improved the national mood. Notably, there were no boos within the 88,000 Wembley crowd at full time, because for half an hour either side of half-time, England dominated the world champions and they played in a very "English" way.

All verve, pace and passion, full of attacking intent. They scored two goals in that period against a side that has only conceded goals to two teams in the last 12 months, and the home side could have scored more in that golden 30 minutes. If only they could sustain that for a full 90 minutes, eh?

Captain Harry Kane told me after the match that this is the mission, having not managed to put in a complete 90-minute performance at the World Cup, and he felt the same was true at Wembley on Saturday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Kane reacts to England's loss against Spain and his penalty miss

What really matters now is how England follow up on this Spain defeat. They have three games in eight days. Three games they ought to win, with Czech Republic home and away sandwiching Croatia away. If they do win all three, it will have been a positive international break, one that very much keeps alive their hopes of making it to the Nations League quarter-finals in the spring. Remember, the top two qualify from each group in League A, and so practically it does not matter if England finish below Spain, so long as they finish above the other two nations.

But once again it is the next game that feels critical for Tuchel. You can imagine the England boss saying to his squad in the post-match debrief: "After the Spanish Inquisition, my friends, comes the test from the Czechs, mates".

Sports.title: Alpine condemn online abuse since Colapinto crash, Norris remarks
Sports.content:
Alpine have condemned the online abuse and hate aimed at drivers and others in Formula 1 since the incident in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that saw Franco Colapinto cause a three-car collision with Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris.

Alpine driver Colapinto triggered the accident in the Baku race's first Safety Car restart when he locked his brakes into the first corner and hit the side of team-mate Gasly, who was sent straight into Norris' McLaren on his outside.

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport," Alpine said as part of a statement issued on Sunday.

All three drivers retired with car damage, with Colapinto apologising to his team-mate, Alpine and Norris for what he admitted had been a "big mistake".

Colapinto will take a five-place grid penalty at this coming week's Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia in lieu of the 10-second time penalty he was unable to serve in the race as he had retired.

Speaking in the immediate aftermath of the incident, a Norris said that drivers who cause incidents like Colapinto did should be banned for one race. The McLaren driver also said "there are some drivers who shouldn't be in Formula 1, to be honest".

Alpine have previously spoken out to condemn online hate from some fans seen following incidents in which Colapinto, who has a big following in Argentina, was involved.

'It has become a regular occurrence and cannot be condoned' - Alpine's statement in full

"As a team, we feel it's necessary to speak out once more about the hate and abuse online following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

"Not only aimed at one of our own drivers, but also members of the Formula One community, including media, and to our racing counterparts who we respect, admire, and revel competing against in the pinnacle of motorsport.

"Mistakes happen when racing at the limit and no matter the result or outcome, nobody should be subject to hateful or abusive comments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Franco Colapinto was apologetic to Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris after he took both out at the first safety car restart

"Condemning abuse on social media is not aimed at any one fan base or the supporters of one team or driver, this is universal and should be called out and recognised to all fans of the sport.

"As we have said in previous instances, we strongly condemn the reaction of some fans online and stand in solidarity with Formula One, the FIA, and other teams in wanting to stamp it out. It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned.

"We know as a proud participant and stakeholder in the sport, we hold a responsibility to speak out and also help support in finding a solution. We will continue to work closely with the championship promoter and rights-holder, and the governing body to discuss ways in which to tackle online abuse and encourage healthy sporting rivalry, which Formula One is renowned for and what makes it so special."

Briatore: I will consider what course of action should be taken with Colapinto

Speaking on Saturday evening about the on-track incident itself, Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore said he would take time "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after Colapinto's "very poor" error.

Gasly had been running a strong seventh at the time, with Colapinto 10th, and the incident cost Alpine what stood as seven points overall.

Stewards' verdict on Colapinto crash "Following the restart, COL approached GAS from behind into Turn 1. COL braked too late and entered the corner on the inside at a speed which did not allow him to make the corner in a controlled manner.



"He overshot the corner and made contact with the left-hand side of GAS, who then hit NOR and both cars retired.



"The Stewards considered that COL was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision.



"Although the incident occurred at the first corner following the restart, there was no contribution from another driver which would justify applying the first-lap / first corner more lenient approach.



"The standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty.



"As COL had retired from the Race and was therefore unable to serve the time penalty, the Stewards converted the penalty to a drop of five grid positions at the next Race in which the driver participates."

With both Alpines and Norris having dropped out ahead of him, Arvid Lindblad instead came through late in the race to finish seventh and stretch Racing Bulls' lead over Alpine in the fight for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship to 15 points with a scheduled eight rounds left.

Speaking in Alpine's official press release issued after the race, Briatore said: "Obviously I'm extremely disappointed with the outcome of today's race, knowing we lost valuable points in the championship fight.

"These sorts of incidents shouldn't happen, particularly when we were running well with both cars in point-scoring positions.

"I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando [Norris] and McLaren for ruining their race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix

"I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart. It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience.

"I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future."

'That's too harsh' - Russell, Verstappen, Hadjar disagree with race ban suggestion

Saturday's top-three finishers in Baku were asked in the post-race press conference about Norris' comments but all agreed that banning a driver for a race for such an incident would be a step too far.

Baku race winner George Russell said: "I think that's too harsh, personally.

"I think Safety Car restarts, cold tyres, a very small mistake can have big consequences.

"And from what I saw today, that's what it looked like. It was a small error that had a big consequence. I think, personally, race bans should come from drivers intentionally doing something very dangerous and very reckless. So I think it was unfortunate."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris hits out after being taken out at the Azerbaijan GP

Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who finished a close second in the race, added: "I think as long as, of course, the driver that caused it is aware of what he did, right, and apologised.

"And, I mean, yeah, that happens. I mean, like, a small mistake or misjudgement, you lock up, it's on the inside, low grip, and, of course, then I guess a bit unfortunate that it involves so many cars.

"But, yeah, unfortunate, happens, and it's not nice, I think. Not nice for anyone involved, right? But like George said, I think, yeah, a race ban probably is a bit much."

Third-place finisher Isack Hadjar agreed with Russell and Verstappen, especially as he felt there were mitigating circumstances in the incident.

"I think the track is not good enough," said the Red Bull driver.

"You move out of the racing line, it starts to be very bumpy. It's hard to generate temperature behind the Safety Car, it's going quite slowly.

"So then, yeah, you just overdo it and then it has big, big consequences. So, I think, yeah, a race ban is way too harsh."

Image: All three drivers retired with car damage

Andrea Stella, Norris' McLaren team boss, said they trusted the stewards to make the right decisions, adding that drivers should also be expected to race with "a certain degree of just common sense".

"It's a complex matter," said Stella before Colapinto's converted grid drop was officially confirmed.

"I guess this is being reviewed by the stewards as we speak, pretty much. I'm sure it will be reviewed by Flavio as well. I'm not sure which one is going to be harsher for whoever caused the problem.

"I think, independently of the dissuasion that you can have because of the penalty, I think when you drive in Formula 1 and you are approaching Turn 1 in Baku and you have seen so many videos of the past, you just should be capitalising on this experience that you should be having as a Formula 1 driver.

"The consequence in this case, which I'm sure, is a shame for Alpine for both drivers, and there's a penalty for other drivers.

"Definitely the penalty should take into account that there are some circuits in which you have to use extra prudency, and there's a full history of problems that happened like this, especially in a street circuit where there's no way to use the runoff area to somehow mitigate the consequences of somebody running onto you.

"We trust the stewards, their approach, but above all, we should trust the drivers that they apply a certain degree of just common sense I would say while driving."

Sports.title: Wakefield hailed after stunning Wigan: 'No team would have competed!'
Sports.content:
Jon Wilkin believes some of the best teams in Super League history would not have beaten Wakefield Trinity on Saturday night, as Daryl Powell's side sealed a huge upset victory against Wigan Warriors to book a spot in the Grand Final.

A flurry of second-half tries saw Trinity end Wigan's 16-match winning streak, with the visitors leaving Matt Peet's side stunned by their ferocious pace and power.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the highlights as Wakefield produced a huge upset against Wigan

Wigan went down to 12 men after 45 minutes, with Adam Keighran being sin-binned for a tip-tackle. Wakefield ruthlessly took advantage, scoring three tries while the Australian five-eighth was off the field.

Wigan did impress in the opening exchanges, matching Wakefield for intensity, with Brad O'Neill breaking the deadlock after a tense first 15 minutes.

But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.

"Wigan were bad, but that was completely induced by what Wakefield threw at them," Wilkin told Sky Sports.

"It was a clinical performance that was full of power, pace, energy, enthusiasm and execution.

"Nobody would have competed with Wakefield today. Not one team in Super League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Trinity scored three tries after Wigan's Adam Keighran was sent to the sin bin for a tip tackle

"I'd go as far as to say some of the great teams we've had in the history of Super League wouldn't have competed with that 80 minutes that Wakefield have dished up."

After Keighran was sent to the bin, Tom Johnston touched down in the corner with a diving finish, before Jack Sinfield beat Junior Nsemba from close range to score another.

They had a third in seven minutes, with Corey Hall sprinting down the wing before smashing his way over the tryline.

Ky Rodwell wrapped up the 27-point win, thanks to some great hands from Jake Trueman.

After the match, Peet lauded Wakefield, adding his Wigan side were "well prepared" but came up second on the night.

"Wakefield were outstandingly good," the Warriors coach said. "All the credit in the world to them, to Daryl. We were outplayed, outcoached, and beaten all ends up.

"Credit to them, it hurts, but the night belongs to them."

A new name on the Super League trophy is now guaranteed, with Trinity to face Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford next Saturday, which is live on Sky Sports.

Powell lauded as top coach

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tom Johnstone scored twice in the match

Powell left his role with Castleford Tigers at the conclusion of the 2021 Super League season, having guided the side to a Challenge Cup final appearance and their maiden Super League Grand Final.

He was appointed head coach at Wakefield in October 2023, and has been instrumental in lifting the club from the Championship to its first Super League Grand Final, after one of their best seasons on record.

"I think the jury was still out after his spell at Castleford," Wilkin said.

"But there is no doubt that Daryl Powell is an exceptional coach, who can get a group of men organised and directed to success.

"That's what he's done, and he's done it with such style and class.

"Wakefield play with risk and they play the game in a beautiful way."

Ellis: I didn't think in my wildest dreams we'd do that

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The victory continues Wakefield's remarkable 2026 season

Wakefield owner Matt Ellis heaped praise on his team following the match:

"It's still not sunk in yet. Four-and-a-half thousand fans still singing away. What a performance.

"That was the best performance in my time owning the club. So proud of them. We just nailed it today, didn't we?

"I didn't think in my wildest dreams [we'd be four scores up].

"I had a good feeling all week about it; all the pressure was on them. We came here, we were confident.

"It's a happy group, but it's an even happier group right now.

"There's so many good stories, three years after relegation, and now we're there!"

Thomas Tuchel’s side embraced the chaos at Wembley and overcame a second-minute Lamine Yamal strike to lead 2-1 at the break thanks to quickfire goals from Anthony Gordon and Kane. The captain then had the chance to make it 3-1, but slipped when taking a penalty that crashed into the crossbar and Spain roared back, taking the three points through Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal. But Kane says his side showed enough to prove they can match the World Cup and European Championship winners. “I think we’re close, without a doubt,” he said. “I think anyone who watched that game will see that. They have the trophies to back it up, so until we do that, we can only use words. We have to show it on the pitch. “We showed a lot of good things on the pitch, but in the big moments, we didn’t quite have it. But we’re top four in the world. We finished third in the World Cup, so without a doubt, we’re close, and I think they would have felt that out there today for sure. “That’s why I think it stings a little bit right now because we know it could have been a different result if we were a little bit cleaner. 4h ago 04.56 EDT Scotland: Sebastien Pocognoli’s reign began with a 0-0 draw with Slovenia yesterday afternoon. It’s a decent first result for Steve Clarke’s successor and gives Scotland a platform to build on before games against Switzerland and North Macedonia in Group B1. Ewan Murray was there to watch … double quotation mark Blue skies, a dainty stadium in Ljubljana and a second-half display that provided glimpses of optimism in respect of Scotland’s world, post-Steve Clarke. The best-forgotten first 45 minutes can be explained away by a squad operating under a new regime. By full time, Slovenia were grateful for their point. Scotland’s players took deserved applause. Scotland’s failing here was a familiar one. A lack of goals haunted Clarke. Nonetheless, this version of Scotland did at least create a series of openings. Scott McTominay, a key attacking threat, was missing. Instilling ruthlessness in a team is no easy task; it is one, however, Pocognoli has the coaching credentials to meet. Slovenia, on this evidence, have the more significant challenges. Pocognoli’s reign as Scotland coach begins with stalemate in Slovenia Read more Share

5h ago 04.46 EDT England: Yes, there was not much he could do about the two defensive errors that led to Spain goals, but there is still something to be said about Thomas Tuchel’s in-game management last night. He seemed to get the initial team selection right – Elliot Anderson and Myles Lewis-Skelly were an effective counter to Rodri and Fabian Ruiz in midfield, while Anthony Gordon was an inspired choice on the left – but the second-half substitutes didn’t have much impact at all. After Harry Kane’s penalty miss on 54 minutes, Luis de la Fuente brought on Alex Baena and Mikel Oyarzabal – two later goalscorers. At 2-2 on 70 minutes, Spain added Pedri to their midfield and England added James Garner, underlining a serious dropoff in strength without the injured Declan Rice. Then the likes of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Morgan Gibbs-White were given little time to affect the game, while replacing Marc Guehi with Jarrad Branthwaite with a minute to go at a goal down seemed fairly pointless.
