He said unregulated waste collection and transportation could undermine the organised waste management system, particularly where waste collected was subsequently dumped at unauthorised locations.

The LAWMA boss also warned against the disposal of waste into waterways, stressing that such practices could undermine the state’s environmental sustainability efforts.

He said: “The Lagos State Government, through LAWMA, will not relent in enforcing environmental regulations across the state.

“These enforcement operations are part of our ongoing efforts to ensure that residents, businesses and waste handlers take responsibility for the proper management and disposal of waste.”

Gbadegesin urged residents, traders and businesses across the state to desist from indiscriminate waste disposal and patronise accredited waste collection operators.

He said waste should be handed over through approved channels, warning that persons found dumping waste on roads, drains, waterways and other unauthorised locations, as well as those engaged in unauthorised waste collection, would face appropriate enforcement action in accordance with applicable laws.

He also urged residents to support LAWMA’s enforcement and waste management operations by maintaining proper waste disposal practices and reporting cases of illegal dumping and unauthorised waste collection through the authority’s established channels.

World.title: Months after concession, ACs fail at Enugu Airport
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Passengers departing the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu, Sunday, lamented the failure of the air-conditioning system in the departure hall, with travellers forced to endure long hours of heat while waiting to board their flights.

The situation was observed by Vanguard, as passengers, including editors leaving Enugu after the 2026 Guild of Editors Conference, were seen sweating in the departure hall.

A passenger, Onyedikachi, who was travelling from Enugu to Lagos, described the situation as unacceptable.

He said: “I got to the departure hall at 10:52 and what I have experienced is unbelievable. Everyone is sweating. This airport was concessioned some months ago, yet it can’t be run efficiently.”

Another passenger, who identified himself simply as Michael, said the situation was embarrassing for an international airport.

He said: “We are at the Enugu Airport. ACs in the departure hall are not working. Horrible. Passengers are sweating. Many of them are editors leaving after the 2026 Guild of Editors Conference. This is an international airport? Who was it concessioned to?”

The development comes barely months after Federal Government handed over the management and operational responsibilities of the airport to Aero Alliance Limited under a Public-Private Partnership arrangement.

The concession, aimed at modernising airport infrastructure, improving operational efficiency and attracting private-sector investment into the aviation sector, was formally signed off in June.

The signing ceremony was announced in a statement by the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, through his Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood.

At the ceremony, Keyamo described the concession as a breakthrough after previous attempts to concession the airport had failed for about two decades.

He said: “This concession plan has been on for about 20 years, but it has only become possible under the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. Before now, investors focused mainly on Lagos, Abuja, and Kano airports. Nobody was interested in Enugu and Port Harcourt. Today, Enugu has been successfully concessioned and Port Harcourt will also be handed over within the next few weeks.”

Keyamo urged Aero Alliance Limited to justify the confidence reposed in it by federal government, saying its performance as one of Nigeria’s pioneer airport concessionaires would serve as a benchmark for future airport concessions.

World.title: Obi questions Tinubu’s absence from UNGA
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has questioned President Bola Tinubu’s absence from the 81st United Nations General Assembly, UNGA, in New York.

Obi raised the issue on Sunday in a post on his X handle after watching an address delivered by Ghanaian President John Dramani Mahama at the global gathering.

In a statement by the spokesman of the Peter Obi Media Office, POMR, Idris Zekeri, the former Anambra State governor asked: “Where is Nigeria’s President?”

Obi, who was the 2023 presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, said he was concerned about Tinubu’s absence from what he described as an important global platform.

He said Nigeria, as Africa’s most populous country, ought to have its President represented at major international engagements.

“Here is the remarkable address delivered by Ghana’s dynamic President, John Dramani Mahama, at the 81st UNGA. As the international community commends this distinguished leader, many are asking: Where is the President of Africa’s most populous nation, a country of more than 200 million people — more than Ghana — whose leader has been absent from the global stage for three consecutive UNGAs?” Obi wrote.

He added: “Nigeria’s President, who ought to be representing and guiding the continent at the international level, has not attended any of these three global gatherings.

“Where is he, particularly at a time when the country faces significant challenges both domestically and internationally?

“Although our Vice President, Kashim Shettima, was present, the question remains: where is the President?”

The Presidency had announced on September 21 that Tinubu had extended his working vacation in Europe by a few days and was expected to return to Nigeria at the weekend.

According to the State House, Tinubu departed Nigeria on August 30 for London to begin the working vacation before proceeding to Paris, France, where he held meetings with French President Emmanuel Macron and businessman Vincent Bollore.

The Presidency also said Tinubu remained in contact with officials at home and continued to direct the affairs of the country while away.

Meanwhile, Vice President Kashim Shettima was mandated to represent Tinubu and lead Nigeria’s delegation to the 81st UNGA.

Shettima subsequently delivered Nigeria’s national statement at the General Debate of the 81st UNGA on Thursday on behalf of the President.

Obi said the circumstances warranted continued prayers for the President’s return and effective leadership in addressing the challenges confronting the country.

“Let us continue to pray for his return and for his leadership in addressing the many challenges confronting the nation, but let us hope that a New Nigeria is possible and will be O-K,” he said.

World.title: LASTMA impounds 84 vehicles over traffic offences
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

LAGOS — The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA, has impounded 84 commercial and private vehicles for various traffic offences during a comprehensive enforcement operation across identified traffic flashpoints in the state.

The exercise, conducted at the weekend around Idumota, Iddo, Ijora-Olopa, Costain and Onipanu, was aimed at restoring order and ensuring compliance with traffic regulations, particularly along corridors where persistent violations by motorists and commercial bus operators have affected the free flow of traffic.

LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, said the agency was particularly concerned about the practice of commercial buses reversing against traffic along the one-way stretch from Iddo to Idumota through Cater Bridge.

According to him, the practice posed serious risks to motorists, commuters and pedestrians using the corridor.

“Motorists and other legitimate road users approaching the bridge may have little or no forewarning that a commercial vehicle is unlawfully reversing against the prescribed direction of traffic, thereby creating an extremely hazardous situation with the potential to precipitate devastating collisions, injuries and fatalities,” he said.

Miscreants attack officers

The enforcement operation, however, reportedly met resistance from some individuals, with LASTMA personnel assaulted and injured while carrying out their duties.

Bakare-Oki confirmed that some alleged miscreants who attacked officers and damaged the agency’s operational vehicles during the exercise were apprehended.

He said the enforcement had become necessary to curb what he described as a growing culture of impunity among some road users and restore discipline along critical traffic corridors.

The LASTMA boss said the agency had repeatedly cautioned transport operators, commercial bus drivers and other road users against using under-bridge spaces, road setbacks and other unauthorised locations as illegal garages.

“We have repeatedly cautioned transport operators, commercial bus drivers and other road users against occupying under-bridge spaces, road setbacks and unauthorised locations as illegal garages as such practices constitute serious impediments to effective traffic management and pose considerable risks to public safety,” he said.

Bakare-Oki said LASTMA would sustain its enforcement campaign to secure compliance with traffic regulations, deter hazardous driving practices and protect the lives and property of motorists, commuters, pedestrians and other road users.

He warned that no individual or group would be allowed to appropriate public roads, bridges or under-bridge spaces for illegal loading, parking, vehicle repairs or garage operations.

He consequently urged commercial bus operators, motorists, transport unions and other stakeholders to desist from one-way driving, dangerous reversing, illegal parking, indiscriminate loading and the occupation of unauthorised garages or under-bridge locations.

He warned that further violations would attract appropriate enforcement measures in accordance with extant Lagos State traffic laws.

The LASTMA boss also urged members of the public to remain vigilant and report dangerous driving, traffic obstructions, reckless motorists and other traffic-related offences through the agency’s toll-free short code, 3367, to enable prompt intervention and prevent avoidable incidents on the state’s road network.

World.title: NDC-UK leadership reaffirms commitment to party
World.content:
Dickson

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The leadership of the United Kingdom Chapter of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, has reaffirmed its commitment to the growth and development of the party following a high-level meeting with its National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, in London.

The NDC-UK Executive Committee paid a courtesy visit to Dickson at the London Park Lane Hilton Hotel on Saturday, where members of the chapter and representatives of the Nigerian community across Great Britain and Ireland interacted with the former Bayelsa State governor.

In a statement on Sunday by the Publicity Secretary of NDC-UK, Boniokoye Imegwu, the meeting provided an opportunity for Dickson to brief party members and supporters on developments within the party, its progress since its formation and preparations for the forthcoming general election.

Dickson was in London on his return to Nigeria from the Netherlands, where he had inaugurated the NDC Netherlands Chapter.

During the interaction, the NDC National Leader expressed confidence in the party’s leadership and presidential ticket.

He also urged institutions and officials responsible for conducting the elections to uphold integrity, fairness, responsibility and patriotism throughout the electoral process.

The NDC-UK Country Chairman, Princewill Urum, thanked Dickson for his leadership and reaffirmed the chapter’s commitment to advancing the objectives and programmes of the party.

Also present at the meeting was the leader of the Coalition for the Protection of Democracy, COPDEM, a Nigerian and global political network.

The COPDEM leader commended what he described as the direction and progress of the NDC, saying the organisation would deploy its available resources and personnel in support of initiatives aimed at promoting democratic participation and a credible electoral process in Nigeria.

Dickson also disclosed that he would return to the United Kingdom later this year with the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi; his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso; and other senior party officials for the formal launch of the NDC-UK Chapter.

The meeting ended on a convivial note, with participants expressing renewed commitment to the expansion of the NDC and its forthcoming electoral activities.

World.title: French loan cannot fund electioneering — Makinde’s aide
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — The Oyo State Government has said the French Treasury Loan secured for its development programme cannot be diverted for electioneering or other purposes outside the scope for which it was approved.

Special Adviser to Governor Seyi Makinde, Mrs Ronke Adedayo, who facilitated the sourcing and acquisition of the facility on behalf of the state government, disclosed this while speaking with journalists at the weekend.

Adedayo said the facility was being implemented in line with the conditions under which it was approved by the French authorities, adding that its financing structure did not permit the state government to divert, reallocate or deploy the funds to projects outside the approved scope.

According to her, the loan operates under a ring-fenced disbursement arrangement, with each tranche tied to specific project milestones and subject to mandatory compliance requirements.

She added that the facility was also subject to compliance audits by relevant French authorities and independent monitors, as well as a restricted expenditure framework designed to ensure that the funds were used only for their approved purposes.

Adedayo said the safeguards prevented the state government from unilaterally changing the purpose of the facility.

She said: “Under these conditions, no government can unilaterally alter the use of the loan, nor can the funds be applied to any project outside the original scope approved by the French Treasury and AFD.

“Any deviation would immediately trigger international compliance violations and halt further disbursement. Those insinuating that the funds might be used for electioneering are merely exhibiting their ignorance.”

The governor’s aide maintained that the Makinde administration remained committed to transparency and compliance with international financing standards throughout the implementation of the facility.

“Just as Governor Seyi Makinde has said, the Oyo State Government remains committed to full transparency and adherence to all international financing standards.

“The French Treasury Loan will continue to be implemented strictly for its designated purpose, in line with global best practices and the development priorities of Oyo State,” she said.

Adedayo also explained why a facility obtained in 2020 was only being accessed in 2026, attributing the delay to the lengthy bureaucratic processes involved in securing the necessary approvals from the Federal Government.

She said the facility was secured on highly concessionary terms, including very low interest rates, which she described as favourable to the state.

The Special Adviser further disclosed that the financing arrangement included a significant French-content component involving the provision of equipment.

According to her, the component was fixed under the agreement and could neither be altered nor tampered with by the state government.

She reiterated that the loan would remain tied to the development programme for which it was approved, with its implementation continuing under the conditions and safeguards attached to the international financing arrangement.

World.title: Why I joined Makinde, Adekanmbi — Ex-Adelabu aide
World.content:
By Adeola Badru

IBADAN — A former Personal Assistant to the erstwhile Minister of Power, Chief Adebayo Adelabu, Ajiboye Akande Sangogade, popularly known as Boye Nation, has explained his decision to leave the All Progressives Congress, APC, for the Allied Peoples Movement, APM.

Sangogade said his decision was based on his personal political conviction and belief in the direction of the APM, stressing that his realignment had nothing to do with any disagreement with his former principal.

Speaking with journalists in Ibadan at the weekend, Sangogade said his decision to support Oyo State Governor, Engr. Seyi Makinde, and the APM governorship candidate, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi, followed his assessment of political developments in the state and his desire to provide a platform for greater participation of young people in politics.

He spoke against the backdrop of the Boye Nation/JAF Movement Mega Concert held at the Lekan Salami Stadium, Adamasingba, Ibadan, where he formally led hundreds of youths, traders, artisans and other supporters from the APC into the APM ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Explaining his decision, Sangogade said he had reached a point where he could no longer remain on the sidelines of the political process, particularly given what he described as the implications of the 2027 elections for the future of young people in Oyo State.

He urged those who had joined the movement to become actively involved in politics rather than remaining passive observers.

“I was a former Personal Assistant (PA) to Chief Adebayo Adelabu. I am not in any way in crisis with anyone. I’m mature enough to make a decision,” he said.

Sangogade stressed that his political movement should not be interpreted as a fallout with Adelabu, maintaining that his decision was independently taken.

“The decision I made has nothing to do with my former boss, Chief Adelabu; it was a decision I took independently,” he said.

He said his political realignment was informed by his assessment of the political environment and his decision to identify with the APM and its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.

According to him, the APM provided an avenue to pursue a new political direction and mobilise young people for greater participation in governance.

The former Adelabu aide declared his support for the APM governorship candidate in Oyo State, Adekanmbi, urging his supporters across the 33 local government areas of the state to rally behind the candidate ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

He urged members of his political structure and other young people to actively participate in the political process, stressing that the outcome of the 2027 elections would have implications for their welfare, empowerment and development.

Sangogade said the political mobilisation was not simply about moving from one political party to another, but about creating an organised platform through which young people could have a stronger voice in determining the leadership of the state and country.

He said the turnout at the Boye Nation/JAF Movement concert demonstrated the level of mobilisation around the APM in Oyo State.

The event, held under the theme, “Young, United, Unstoppable (YUU),” attracted supporters and formally marked the reception of Sangogade and his supporters into the APM.

World.title: Kidnapping, Gun-Running, Drug Trade: Workers seek logistics regulation
World.content:
File image

By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Henry Obetta

Workers in Nigeria’s courier and logistics sector have called for urgent regulation of the industry, warning that weak oversight is exposing the sector and the country to security and economic risks.

The workers, under the aegis of the Courier and Logistics Staff Association of Nigeria, CALSSAN, made the call at the union’s First Quadrennial Delegate Conference in Lagos.

The conference had as its theme, “Steering the Logistics Terrain in Nigeria – Importance and Necessity of Regulatory Framework for the Industry.”

Speaking at the event, CALSSAN President, Mr Festus Oluwatuyi, identified inadequate regulation as one of the major challenges confronting the industry.

He said, “Majorly, we want government to look into the regulation. In the courier and service industry in Nigeria, there is no regulation.”

Oluwatuyi also appealed to the government to improve road infrastructure, stressing that logistics operators depended heavily on the nation’s road network.

He said, “We pray the government improve on the infrastructure because the other name for our business is transport. We move on the road.”

The CALSSAN president further alleged that some employers were preventing workers from joining the union, insisting that the association remained committed to protecting workers’ rights.

He said, “We are serious and we are focused on ensuring that those employees have their fundamental human rights.”

Also speaking, Mr Osita Nweke, Country Head, Business Development, United Parcel Service, UPS, said the absence of effective regulation had left the industry vulnerable to abuse.

According to him, the sector had become an “all-commerce affair”, with unregistered operators providing courier and logistics services without adequate oversight.

He said such gaps could create security risks, alleging that some unregulated operators had been linked to kidnapping, gun-running and drug distribution.

Nweke said, “It has become an all-commerce affair where you have people who are not really registered providing services to the people. They are not regulated and that’s why it could be a security risk also for the country.

“That’s why you could have cases of disparate guys kidnapping kids. Some of them are into gun running. Some of them, like recently, we found out you have people who are even into drugs also distributing drugs within the metropolis because the regulatory agencies are weak in terms of enforcing regulation.”

He also stressed the importance of infrastructure to the growth of the sector, saying improved road networks would strengthen the supply chain and boost commerce.

Nweke said, “If the infrastructural architecture of the country is improved on, supply chain would thrive because supply chain is the heartbeat of commerce.”

He added that poor roads could severely disrupt the movement of goods and services.

“For a journey that could take less than eight hours, you see people spending two days on the road. It affects supply chain,” he said.

Representing Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, the Commissioner for Establishment and Training, Mr Afolabi Ayantayo, assured logistics operators of the state government’s support.

Ayantayo said providing the necessary infrastructure would enable operators to conduct their businesses peacefully, efficiently and effectively.

He said, “When you have infrastructure in place for people to do their businesses, especially people that are in logistics business… we make it possible for them to do business in peace, quickly and efficiently.

“The promise of Lagos State government to people in this very industry is that we are going to satisfy the logistics operators.”

The Lagos State Chairman of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, Mrs Agnes Sessi, who represented the NLC President, Mr Joe Ajaero, said the organisation of logistics workers was important to both employees and employers.

She said the union would not only strengthen workers but also contribute to stronger organisations within the sector.

Sessi called for enduring policies and infrastructure to support businesses in the courier and logistics industry.

“We need policies, enduring policies that will support the businesses in the courier and logistics sector. We need infrastructures,” she said.

Also speaking, IT Director, DHL, Kingsley David, who represented the Managing Director of DHL, Muyiwa Adesoju, urged stakeholders to work together to address challenges confronting the sector.

He said, “The recommendation will always be that all logistics companies come together and be able to harness their strengths because there’s always strength in unity.”

David also called on the government to create an enabling environment for logistics businesses, particularly through improved infrastructure.

He said, “When it rains, the roads are flooded. So in terms of infrastructure, that it is available and they are also able to support the kind of business that we do.”

Representing the Minister of Labour and Employment, Muhammad Maigari Dingiyadi, the Registrar of Trade Unions, Mr Shaibu Rabiu, urged CALSSAN’s leadership to prioritise workers’ welfare and due process.

Rabiu also urged the new leadership to formulate programmes and policies that would have a direct impact on members.

The conference brought together labour leaders, logistics operators and other stakeholders, who called for stronger regulation, improved infrastructure and better protection for workers in Nigeria’s courier and logistics industry.

World.title: Tinubu Felicitates Bishop Oyedepo At 72
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has felicitated the Founder and Presiding Bishop of Living Faith Church Worldwide, Bishop David Olaniyi Oyedepo, on his 72nd birthday on September 27, 2026.

The president, in a statement issued on Sunday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, joined the Oyedepo family, Living Faith Church Worldwide, the Christian community and millions of Bishop Oyedepo’s admirers in celebrating a life devoted to faith, service, leadership and human development.

Tinubu acknowledged Bishop Oyedepo’s remarkable contributions to the moral and spiritual development of individuals and communities, particularly his consistent emphasis on integrity, discipline, diligence, responsibility and excellence.

He noted the Bishop’s longstanding advocacy for values that strengthen families, institutions, and nations, and his message of hope, purpose, and personal responsibility, which has resonated with people across Nigeria and beyond.

The president commended Bishop Oyedepo’s significant contributions to education and human-capital development through institutions such as Covenant University and Landmark University, which have provided platforms for academic excellence, leadership development, entrepreneurship and innovation.

According to Tinubu, “Bishop Oyedepo’s influence extends beyond the pulpit into education, publishing, leadership development and humanitarian service, with the Living Faith Church maintaining a significant international presence across Africa and other parts of the world.

“For over four decades of ministry, Bishop Oyedepo has become a prominent Nigerian voice on faith, leadership, integrity, education and human development, with his books and teachings reaching audiences across national and continental boundaries.

“Bishop Oyedepo has devoted decades to preaching faith, promoting integrity and encouraging excellence, while investing substantially in education and the development of human capacity. His commitment to building lives, institutions and communities has given his ministry a significant national and international footprint.

“I especially salute Bishop Oyedepo for the social-development initiatives, including schools, healthcare facilities, and humanitarian interventions, associated with his ministry and the David Oyedepo Foundation’s support for education and people in need.

“On this auspicious occasion of his 72nd birthday, I celebrate his life of service and pray that Almighty God will continue to grant him wisdom, strength, good health and renewed grace as he advances the cause of faith, education, morality and human development.

“I wish Bishop Oyedepo many more years of fulfilment, good health and continued service to God and humanity.”
