World.title: International coalition halts financial aid to Peshmerga
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US-led international coalition has officially halted financial aid to Iraqi Kurdistan’s Peshmerga forces following the expiration of a four-year agreement.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and the United States Department of Defense inked an agreement that extended from September 21, 2022, until September 21, 2026.

On Thursday, the troops received their final allowance for August and September 2026.

According to the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs, Bakhtiar Sadiq, the financial aid under the initial agreement was planned to steadily reduce by 25 percent each year until reaching a complete halt.

This cash halt aligns with the overall conclusion of the international coalition’s military operations in Iraq, with a full stoppage of combat and training responsibilities expected by September 30, 2026.

Additionally, the proposed US Counter-ISIS Train and Equip Fund (CTEF) plan for 2027 includes no support for the Peshmerga.

The international coalition has tied its financial assistance to necessary reforms and the unification of the Peshmerga forces, particularly the integration of politically separated units. Earlier in September, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) publicly announced that the unification process was complete.

To address the newly established funding imbalance, the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs has formally requested the federal government in Baghdad to adjust Peshmerga salaries to align them permanently with federal Iraqi military and security forces.

World.title: Iraq seeks US exemption to resume Iranian flights
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government revealed on Saturday that it is holding discussions with the US administration to obtain an exemption for certain Iraqi airports from the ban on Iranian airline flights imposed under US sanctions, citing the disruption caused to traveling patients, students, and pilgrims.

According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the Iraqi government is engaged in direct talks with the US side to exempt specific Iraqi airports from these measures.

The exception would allow for the resumption of flights for humanitarian grounds, which include medical care, education, religious pilgrimages, and civilian interests.

Iranian airlines primarily handle the transport of Iranians traveling to Iraq in large numbers to visit the shrines of Shiite Imams, as well as Iraqis flying to Iran for religious pilgrimages, studies, or medical treatment.

Iraq joined several other nations in suspending Iranian flights to and from its territory after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that all Iranian airlines will cease operations as of September 23.

Under the new measures, any country or firm that provides services to Iranian aircraft is completely removed from the global US dollar system. The services include fueling airplanes, offering ground handling and landing services, and selling passenger tickets.

World.title: Iraq unveils plan for data centers in Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications unveiled an ambitious strategic blueprint on Saturday, September 26, 2026, to construct a distributed network of enterprise data centers across Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul, aiming to upgrade national digital infrastructure and localize hosting for global technology conglomerates.

In an exclusive statement granted to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the Director General of the General Company for Communications and Informatics, Ali Yassin, confirmed that establishing tier-standard data centers across multiple provinces stands among the ministry’s top executive priorities to accelerate digital transformation.

Yassin revealed that the capital city of Baghdad will host three dedicated data centers situated across prime connectivity hubs, specifically at the Al-Sinak telecommunications complex, the Al-Intisar facility, and the Al-Mamoun Telecommunications Tower compound adjacent to the ministry’s headquarters.

The geographical distribution within the capital ensures redundant network routing, continuous uptime, and high-speed fiber interconnection to support both federal e-governance platforms and commercial cloud services.

Beyond Baghdad, the national strategy targets key regional logistics and transit corridors, including a specialized facility planned in Basra Governorate in close proximity to the international submarine cable landing station, directly capitalizing on Iraq’s high-capacity maritime fiber-optic gateways.

Additionally, the ministry is preparing to establish another facility in Mosul to anchor cloud architecture across the northern provinces.

Yassin emphasized that these specialized data centers are purpose-built to attract major multinational technology companies, creating localized environments capable of hosting global content, accelerating low-latency data delivery, and reinforcing Iraq’s sovereign digital ecosystem.

World.title: Iraq reaches 100,000 LPG converted cars as Parliament urges factory model access
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Gas Filling and Services Company, an operating affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Oil, announced on Saturday, September 26, 2026, that the cumulative number of vehicles converted to run on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has reached approximately 100,000 across Iraq.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the company’s media director, Mahdi Al-Nouri, confirmed that retrofitted vehicle figures currently range between 98,000 and 100,000 cars, noting an escalating pace of adoption among motorists seeking economical alternatives to conventional liquid fuels.

Al-Nouri stated that installation and technical maintenance services are carried out across a nationwide network of 26 specialized workshops operating under the state-owned gas company.

The growing consumer uptake reflects heightened public interest in cleaner, subsidized autogas, prompting the Ministry of Oil to scale up workshop throughput and expand fueling station capacity to keep up with escalating demand.

Despite this milestone, converted vehicles represent a modest fraction—less than 1.5 percent—of Iraq’s national automobile fleet, which currently totals approximately 7 million registered cars. The autogas initiative has simultaneously sparked parliamentary scrutiny regarding regulatory bottlenecks.

Lawmaker Amer Abdul-Jabbar raised the issue on the floor of the Council of Representatives, criticizing the Ministry of Oil for restricting autogas dispensing exclusively to locally converted vehicles while denying fuel to imported cars equipped with factory-installed LPG systems.

Abdul-Jabbar called on the federal government to reform existing fuel distribution policies, authorize gas sales for all compatible vehicles, and incentivize the commercial importation of factory-built LPG cars to accelerate emissions reduction and alleviate domestic gasoline consumption.

World.title: Iraq launches first smart pneumatic waste collection system with Spanish backing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC), in coordination with the Ministry of Environment and the Spanish Embassy in Baghdad, officially launched the country’s first smart automated pneumatic waste collection system (URD) on Saturday, September 26, 2026, marking a pivotal milestone in the modernization of municipal sanitation and sustainable urban management.

The initiative introduces advanced underground vacuum collection networks designed to eliminate conventional curbside dumpsters and heavy collection vehicular traffic across newly planned smart cities and licensed residential investment developments.

Speaking at the launch conference attended by an Iraqi News Agency (INA) correspondent, NIC Deputy Chairman Salar Mohammed Amin affirmed that the adoption of the URD pneumatic network represents a comprehensive national initiative requiring deep cross-institutional synergy between public ministries, municipal directorates, and private developers.

He revealed that the commission has already secured all statutory and regulatory approvals to mandate the underground system within master plans for new satellite cities and residential complexes, establishing a national technical committee alongside the Ministry of Environment to oversee phased execution and enforce strict environmental compliance benchmarks.

Amin emphasized that sustainable investment must transcend structural brick-and-mortar construction to create integrated, livable urban ecosystems that elevate daily public health and quality of life.

He noted that operational success relies on an interconnected institutional network encompassing the Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works, the Municipality of Baghdad, local governorate authorities, the Ministry of Electricity, and telecommunications operators, working collectively to provide dedicated power grids, subterranean civil infrastructure, and smart sensor integration necessary for automated municipal services.

Spanish Ambassador to Iraq Alicia Rico Pérez del Pulgar underscored that the rollout of the pneumatic vacuum infrastructure represents a substantial qualitative leap toward modernizing waste management practices through cleaner, more energy-efficient technologies.

Highlighting Madrid’s dedication to technical knowledge transfer and bilateral capacity building, the ambassador framed the project as a catalyst for expanded Spanish-Iraqi commercial and environmental partnerships in green infrastructure, renewable energy, and smart city urban planning, calling upon public institutions and private enterprises from both nations to leverage the project into enduring bilateral economic cooperation.

World.title: Iraq secures new US dollar cash shipment following Al Zaidi’s New York talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi reached formal understandings with U.S. authorities to secure the regular delivery of physical U.S. dollar cash shipments to Iraq, following bilateral and multilateral engagements alongside U.S. President Donald Trump in New York.

Government spokesperson Haider Al-Aboudi confirmed the development on Saturday, September 26, 2026, in an official statement reported by the 964 Network, indicating that high-level diplomatic contacts helped unblock logistical pipelines governing foreign currency transfers to the Central Bank of Iraq.

Al-Aboudi stated that a new installment of physical dollar currency is slated to arrive in Baghdad within the coming days, replenishing sovereign foreign exchange reserves and reinforcing domestic market liquidity.

The government spokesman emphasized that the agreement directly reflects substantial structural progress achieved by Iraqi monetary and fiscal authorities in tightening regulatory control over foreign currency distribution channels, enhancing transparency through the electronic trading platform, and preventing the illicit diversion of commercial liquidity.

The impending cash arrival comes at a critical juncture for Iraq’s parallel currency markets, where the dinar has steadily recovered toward the 157,000 range per $100 after trading near 160,000 earlier in September.

Iraqi financial officials anticipate that the scheduled cash injections, combined with comprehensive regulatory compliance recognized during the New York meetings, will help bridge the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory peg of 131,000 dinars per $100 and stabilize domestic commodity pricing across the country.

World.title: AI startup urges optimism from Europe despite safety fears
World.content:
Freiburg im Breisgau – Europe needs to view artificial intelligence with more optimism — despite growing warnings about its dangers — or risk falling further behind, the head of a leading European AI start-up warned.

“I think the mindset in Europe needs to shift to one of optimism and to one of opportunity, and not to one of risk and fear,” Robin Rombach, CEO of German AI image generation specialist Black Forest Labs, told AFP.

Europe lags behind the United States and China when it comes to cutting-edge AI models. Policymakers and firms have been scrambling to find ways to make up lost ground.

But the debate has shifted to safety in recent weeks, after security lapses sparked calls from some industry leaders for development of the technology to be slowed down.

Based in the medieval German city of Freiburg, Rombach’s company — which takes its name from the nearby Black Forest — has emerged as a prominent developer of AI image-generation models.

The startup, valued at around $3.25 billion, recently hit the headlines when it announced US director Martin Scorsese as an advisor, prompting an angry response from some in Hollywood concerned about AI taking production jobs.

Rombach, 33, helped develop latent diffusion, a breakthrough that underpins many of today’s AI image-generation systems.

This propelled Rombach and a group of fellow computer scientists to found the AI lab in 2024. With just over 100 staff, its FLUX models generate still and moving images from text, and the company is now also expanding into physical AI.

Its latest model has been tested at carmaker Audi as part of a project aimed at enabling robots to perform production-line tasks.

Despite its roots in Freiburg — Rombach comes from the area — the firm’s ties to the United States and its tech scene are also strong.

The company has a second headquarters in San Francisco and secured early backing from Silicon Valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz.

– ‘Stupidity’ is biggest risk –

Rombach said that when Black Forest Labs was founded, there was no “real startup ecosystem” in Europe, particularly for “frontier deep tech”.

“If you want to build a frontier model in a very competitive space, you need to do this quickly.”

“Certain ingredients” are needed for success, such as a lot of capital and computing power, he added.

As well as Black Forest Labs, Europe has other competitive AI companies, including France’s Mistral, but is still seen as trailing US firms such as OpenAI and Anthropic and Chinese labs such as DeepSeek.

Zach Meyers of CERRE, a Brussels-based think tank, echoed some of Rombach’s concerns, saying the “biggest barrier” to AI growth and innovation in Europe was access to capital.

Most European companies rely on financing from banks, which are traditionally more cautious than venture capital investors about backing businesses that may take years to become profitable, said Meyers, an expert in EU digital policy.

“That is not how technology markets work, particularly with a really nascent technology like AI,” he told AFP.

Safety concerns related to AI have escalated after incidents of the technology getting around controls during tests, sparking dire warnings from some about the threats that it poses.

Rombach emphasised his company’s focus on “open-weight” AI models, some of which can be downloaded by researchers and developers, “increases transparency, increases safety”.

He called for an open approach to AI development, warning it would be “fundamentally wrong” for such a crucial technology to be controlled by a few companies, rendering oversight more difficult.

But for Rombach, the biggest danger rests in potential human failings.

“The main thing that can wipe out humanity is stupidity,” he said.

World.title: Japanese anime actor fights TikTok over AI voice cloning
World.content:
Tokyo – A high-profile Japanese anime voice actor has taken TikTok to court over videos he says feature an artificial intelligence clone of his “lustrous” baritone, with a verdict due on Wednesday.

AI imitation is a growing concern among performers worldwide, and the threat has roiled Japan’s storied animation industry, whose voice actors are sometimes worshipped as much as their characters by fans.

The lawsuit filed by Kenjiro Tsuda, known for his starring roles in mega-franchises including “Jujutsu Kaisen” and “Yu-Gi-Oh!”, is believed to be the country’s first seeking to defend an individual’s vocal identity against AI-generated copies.

Tsuda is demanding TikTok remove a slew of videos narrated by a distinctively “deep” and “lustrous” voice that the 55-year-old says can only be his.

The platform however argues it is a “generic male voice” whose perceived similarity to Tsuda’s is subjective at best, according to court records accessed by AFP.

An actor’s voice “is the result of years of rigorous training and apprenticeship” to hone talent, Yuko Sasaki, executive director of the Japan Actors Union, told AFP.

“It’s something we spend lots of time and money perfecting,” said Sasaki, a fellow voice actor, adding that “we support Tsuda wholeheartedly”.

The court should “acknowledge that ownership of a voice is a fundamental right”, she said.

An anonymous account, whose picture resembled a “Jujutsu Kaisen” character dubbed by Tsuda, posted the videos in question.

They combined images and seemingly AI-generated speech about urban legends, occult phenomena and conspiracy theories.

The account at one point boasted more than 200,000 subscribers and would have brought in upwards of 500,000 yen ($3,200) in monthly revenue, the legal complaint argued.

– ‘Sordid content’ –

The account, whose posts mostly lacked original substance, “only gained popularity because its dubious, sordid content was narrated by the attractive voice of a popular actor,” Tsuda’s legal team said, according to the court records.

This infringes Tsuda’s so-called publicity rights — the ability to control and profit from the use of aspects of one’s identity — his attorneys said.

Although the account itself is no longer viewable on the platform, the Tokyo District Court will rule on whether TikTok was responsible for deleting the posts.

Parallel to the lawsuit, Sasaki and other Japanese voice actors have launched a campaign, called “No More”, against using generative AI to mimic performers without permission.

“Our industry can be crushed” if a court win for TikTok triggers “unbridled” AI voice cloning on social media, actor Bin Shimada told AFP.

That could cause younger actors to “lose hope”, said Shimada, who is part of the campaign group.

It is also fast becoming a global issue.

“In many countries copyright and data protection laws are not being adequately adapted” to protect performers from AI clones, the International Federation of Actors said last year.

ChatGPT maker OpenAI was forced to apologise in 2024 to star Scarlett Johansson over a synthetic voice that sounded like her, released after she declined to work with OpenAI on the project.

– International interest –

While no law explicitly enshrines a person’s voice in Japan, the justice ministry published legally non-binding guidelines last month clarifying its protection under existing rights.

As “the symbol of one’s personality” voice is subject to “publicity rights” and “rights to prevent unauthorised use of one’s portrait and likeness”, the ministry said.

But it remains to be seen whether and how the guidelines will influence Wednesday’s court decision on Tsuda’s case.

TikTok has questioned the actor’s “national fame”, rejecting his accusations that the account was free-riding on a well-known brand in a violation of Japan’s unfair competition prevention laws.

As a platform, all it did was “host a forum where users could post creative and ingenious content within the scope of free speech,” it told the court.

It is “very unlikely” that Tsuda’s voice will be outright denied publicity rights, Tatsuhiro Ueno, a professor of intellectual property studies at Waseda University, told AFP.

Given the actor’s “Jujutsu Kaisen” role as a stoic, elite sorcerer that made his voice “highly recognisable in Europe”, Ueno believes the verdict “will garner a lot of international interest”.

Veteran voice actor Michihiro Ikemizu, 83, also expressed solidarity with Tsuda — but said that AI, however sophisticated it gets, will never outperform human actors.

“You need to constantly feel and adapt while performing your role. That’s something AI can never do,” Ikemizu told AFP.

“That’s our only weapon.”

World.title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTA’s confidential exam areas
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

(NTA) has tightened security around its examination work with 39

personnel deployed at its New Delhi office. The force will monitor confidential areas, control access and screen staff and visitors.

The move follows repeated questions over paper leaks and administrative lapses, including the handling of sensitive examination material.

The CISF personnel have been deployed at entry and exit points of the confidential areas at the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. They will carry out access-control and screening measures, including frisking with X-ray baggage screening machines and Door Frame Metal Detectors (DFMDs).

The NTA has also demarcated confidential areas within its new premises. Movement and operations in these areas will be closely monitored as part of efforts to prevent unauthorised access to examination material.

"Confidential areas have been demarcated in the building where the movement and operations will be strictly monitored to ensure that a foolproof system is in place. The Home Ministry has approved Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) security cover for the premises," a senior official said.





NTA shifts sensitive operations to new office

The security measures come after the NTA moved its confidential and sensitive operations from its earlier office in Okhla to a new facility on Minto Road.

"A dedicated over 55,000 square feet office space has been allotted in the Government of India Press Building on Minto Road. The fifth floor and parts of the fourth and sixth floors of the said building have been allotted to the National Testing Agency. Confidential and sensitive operations have been shifted in the last one month to the newly allotted building," the official said.

Other parts of the Government of India Press Building are already protected by the CISF. The NTA will now have a dedicated security arrangement for its examination-related confidential areas.

The agency's new security framework also includes tighter monitoring of examination-critical technology systems. The NTA is working on strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage.

"Arrangements are being made in mission mode for establishing strict access controls, encryption standards, immutable logging and tamper-evident storage for all examination-critical workloads."

Cybersecurity measures being strengthened

The NTA is also reviewing the security of systems used throughout the examination cycle. These include candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing, OMR processing, result systems and other examination-supporting infrastructure.

"Running security readiness reviews of all examination-supporting systems before each examination cycle in coordination with NTA's technology function and coordinating with NTA's test-security function on the technical security of examination day workflows -- including biometric authentication, face-matching, CCTV systems and live monitoring infrastructure -- are among the action items being worked upon," the official said.

The agency is also preparing an examination-specific cyber-incident response system. It plans to have enhanced security operations centre monitoring and rapid-response capabilities on examination days.

The NTA has designated a dedicated chief information security officer (CISO) to oversee information security.

"The position of general manager and CISO has been advertised, and the selection process is at an advanced stage.

Independent third-party cyber-security audits by CERT-In and C-DAC empanelled agencies continue to be undertaken," the official said.

Paper leak exposed gaps in confidential section

The latest security measures follow the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak, which triggered nationwide student protests and brought scrutiny on the NTA's examination processes.

A CBI chargesheet identified three subject experts as the primary sources of the leaked paper. According to the chargesheet, experts entering the NTA's confidential section were not checked or frisked during entry or exit.

The experts were allegedly able to take briefs from the question papers on small chits made from plain sheets provided to them for rough work and translation.

The CBI also noted that the NTA did not have a dedicated CCTV live-feed monitoring control room in its Delhi office. This meant the activities of the three accused experts went unnoticed.

The NTA was established in 2017 under the Ministry of Education to conduct fair, transparent and standardised examinations.

Earlier reforms and fresh scrutiny

The 2024 NEET paper leak had also led to the setting up of a high-level committee headed by former ISRO chairman K Radhakrishnan. The panel recommended stronger security controls across the examination process.

Its recommendations covered question paper systems, candidate registration, fee payment, admit cards, computer-based testing platforms, OMR processing, normalisation engines and result systems.

A separate high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani was also announced to recommend reforms to make the examination system leakproof. The panel was set up after the controversy and is yet to submit its report.

Following the 2026 paper leak, the Supreme Court reprimanded the NTA, saying "it has not learnt its lessons".

The latest security overhaul therefore extends beyond physical protection of confidential material. The agency is now combining CISF security, tighter access controls, CCTV and live monitoring with cybersecurity audits and technical safeguards across its examination systems.

World.title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government on Sunday withdrew its notification exempting the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information Act, hours after issuing the Gazette notification that classified the department as an "Intelligence and Security Organisation".

The rollback came after the move drew criticism from political leaders, including Congress's Karti P Chidambaram and BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan. The government, however, did not publicly cite a specific reason for issuing the exemption or explain why it was withdrawn. An official communication later confirmed that the order issued under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act had been rescinded, reported ANI.

What was the notification?

The original notification, issued by the Human Resources Management Department and published in the state Gazette, used the power available to state governments under Section 24(4) of the RTI Act.

The provision allowed a state government to notify an organisation established by it as an intelligence or security organisation, thereby taking it outside the normal scope of the RTI Act.

Tamil Nadu's notification designated its Public (Law and Order) Department as such an organisation. Had it remained in force, routine RTI access to a broad range of records held by the department would have been restricted.

The records covered included information relating to communal and caste clashes, political agitations, police action and custody, deaths of prisoners, police firing, inquiries into law-and-order incidents and requests for withdrawal of cases arising from political or communal tensions.





The exemption was not absolute. Section 24 specifically preserves access to information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the Act.

The notification itself invoked Section 24(4) and classified the department as an intelligence and security organisation. The government has not, in the material available publicly gave a detailed explanation for why the Public (Law and Order) Department was brought under this provision.

The department handles sensitive law-and-order and policing-related matters, which appears to be the basis on which the exemption was framed. But that is distinct from saying that the government officially justified the move on a particular security ground. The notification, as reported, simply exercised the statutory power under Section 24(4).

The backlash

The proposed exemption would have affected access to records concerning issues such as police firing, custodial deaths, torture, communal and caste clashes and politically sensitive cases, prompting criticism that the move could reduce transparency.

Karti Chidambaram initially criticised the decision, saying it "does not set a good precedent" and recalling that the RTI Act was enacted by the UPA government to strengthen democratic accountability.

"The Law and Order Department handles crucial matters such as examining inquiry reports on police firing, custodial deaths, torture, and deaths of remand prisoners, security-related detention cases, communal and caste clash reports, requests for withdrawal of politically sensitive cases and matters relating to sanction of prosecution for defamatory articles, news items, and speeches.

This crucial information is now being shielded from the public.

Such rollbacks are not in line with transparent governance. RTI must be expanded, not restricted," Chidambaram posted on X.

After the government withdrew the notification, he welcomed the decision, saying: "My unsolicited & friendly advice to the TVK Government & CMO Tamil Nadu â don't let bureaucrats set the tone, tenor & direction of the administration."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

BJP's Tamilisai Soundararajan also criticised the original notification, saying: "So they are afraid of meeting the press, they are afraid of meeting the people, and they are afraid of the legal procedures. If you are free and fair, why are you afraid of RTI?" She called the move "undemocratic" and said it should be "highly condemned."

With the withdrawal of the notification, the Public (Law and Order) Department is no longer covered by the newly created exemption.

The RTI Act, 2005, establishes a legal framework for citizens to access information held by public authorities, subject to exemptions specified in the law.

World.title: When ‘secret spot’ goes viral: The tourism trap of too many views, too many visitors
World.content:
Tourism brings people, places, and cultures closer. It creates opportunities for communities, supports livelihoods, and contributes significantly to economic development.

Globally, travel and tourism contributed $10.9 trillion, or 10% of global GDP, in 2024, supporting 357 million jobs and generating $1.9 trillion in international visitor spending.

But the way people decide where to go is changing - and increasingly, the journey begins before the journey, inside a phone.

On World Tourism Day 2026, observed on September 27, the global tourism sector is discussing how digital technology and Artificial Intelligence can redesign tourism.

India arrives at that conversation amid extraordinary growth: Domestic Tourist Visits reached 428.55 crore in 2025, up from 67.7 crore in 2021, while Foreign Tourist Visits rose from 0.1 crore to 2.53 crore. Foreign Exchange Earnings from tourism increased from Rs 63,978 crore to Rs 2,76,831 crore over the same period, according to the Ministry of Tourism.

The opportunity is enormous. So, is the question increasingly confronting destinations: what happens when a beautiful place becomes more famous online than it is capable of being on the ground?

That is the emerging Instagram destination problem.





From travel guide to visual trigger

Instagram Reels have fundamentally changed travel discovery. A 20-second video can compress a mountain road, turquoise lake, cafÃ©, waterfall or village into an irresistible sequence of drone shots, music, transitions and carefully selected frames.

The Government of India has itself recognised social media's growing role in tourism. A Ministry of Tourism study titled âSocial Media as an Influencer among Foreign Tourists Visiting Indiaâ, conducted through the Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management, examined social media's influence on foreign visitors.

The ministry subsequently acknowledged the importance of Instagram, YouTube, influencers, vloggers and user-generated content in tourism promotion. Tourism policy expert Hemant Joshi, CEO of Atithi Foundation, says the challenge is that visitor demand can grow far faster than a destinationâs infrastructure, carrying capacity and local ecosystem can handle. âWe are increasingly seeing this in fragile mountain and rural destinations, where a viral post can almost instantly translate into traffic, waste, pressure on water and other local infrastructure, and disruption for communities.

Recent experiences in places such as Manali, Ladakh and the Nilgiris are a reminder of this gap,â he said.

A viral viewpoint

Once someone interacts with travel content, similar destinations can flood their feed. Discovery therefore becomes less deliberate. A person who has never heard of a particular valley, cafÃ© or viewpoint can encounter it repeatedly until an unfamiliar place starts feeling like a destination they need to experience.

The algorithm loves the photogenic

The problem is not that social media makes people travel. Travel inspiration has always existed.

The difference is scale, speed and concentration. Algorithms reward content that attracts attention. Visually dramatic places are naturally suited to short-form video. That creates a feedback loop:

beautiful destination â engaging Reel â high views â more creators â more travellers â more content â even more visibility.

Travel enthusiast and hotel manager working in Gurgaon, Nitish Srivastava, who also creates travel content, says algorithms have a soft spot for what already grabs eyeballs. âSo creators can end up repeatedly visiting the same popular places because they know the audience will respond,â he added.

He said a creator can show the experience of a fragile place without necessarily turning its precise location into a mass-tourism instruction manual.

âYou can still share the experience without turning it into a âgo here before everyone finds outâ trend. For me, protecting a place is more important than getting a few extra views,â Nitish said.

Delhi-based traveller Harsh Shivam, who likes sharing travel-related content on social media, similarly argues that creators should exercise judgement when revealing particularly fragile or previously uncrowded locations.

âLocation is obviously an important part of travel content, but there is a difference between telling people roughly where a place is and giving them precise directions to a spot that may not be able to handle a sudden influx of visitors,â said Harsh.

But he also highlights the other side: âIncreased tourism can create opportunities for local businesses and communities.ââ

That is the central paradox.

Visibility can be economic development. The same visibility can become environmental pressure.

Can an algorithm create overtourism?

The reel doesn't show the queue

There is another problem: social media shows a destination, but rarely shows its carrying capacity. A reel might capture the waterfall. It probably won't show the road leading to it clogged with vehicles.

It might show a pristine mountain lake. It probably won't show the plastic waste left behind.

It might show an empty viewpoint. It won't necessarily tell you that the shot was taken at 6 am, during a brief window between crowds.

âA place may only look the way it does in a particular season, or the experience may change significantly depending on the time of year. That context can be important in setting realistic expectations for people planning a visit,â said Harsh.

Srivastava says his own experience has repeatedly demonstrated this gap: âSocial media usually shows the best few secondsâthe perfect light, empty viewpoint and cinematic angle.â

When the road becomes the bottleneck

India's tourism numbers make this increasingly important.

Official Uttarakhand statistics show how dramatically visitor numbers can concentrate at individual destinations. Kedarnath recorded 243,012 visitors in 2021, rising to 1,564,248 in 2022 and 1,958,863 in 2023. Badrinath rose from 199,409 in 2021 to 1,780,429 in 2023. Tehri recorded more than 3.76 million tourist visits in 2023, according to Uttarakhand Tourism.

The issue isn't simply how many people enter a state. It is where they go, when they arrive and whether local infrastructure can absorb the concentration. Roads, parking, public toilets, accommodation, drinking water, sewage systems, emergency services and waste collection all have finite capacity. And when tourism growth is faster than infrastructure, the first visible sign may not be a tourism statistic. It may be a traffic jam.

Too Viral to Handle

The environmental bill arrives later

Government research shows that the environmental consequences are not theoretical.

A Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change report submitted before the National Green Tribunal documented significant waste pressures associated with tourism in Uttarakhand. Research cited in the report, in January 2025 found that 71% of the total solid waste generated in the Valley of Flowers was produced in only 37 days.

Estimated waste generation was approximately 364 grams per visitor per day on the Gomukh trek and 580 grams per visitor per day on the Kedarkantha trek.

These numbers reveal an important characteristic of tourism pollution: seasonality and concentration matter.

A place can cope with relatively modest visitor numbers for much of the year and still experience severe pressure during a short viral or peak-tourism window.

Ladakh offers another stark example. A carrying-capacity study by the GB Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment examined tourism pressure in the Leh Town Complex. The research recorded rapid growth in accommodation, air traffic and tourist influx, alongside concerns over waste generation and disposal. Ladakh's ecological vulnerability makes the equation particularly sensitive. Water, waste treatment, roads and energy are not infinitely expandable simply because Instagram demand rises.

According to Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat data obtained through an RTI, Kedarnath generated 50.30 metric tonnes of waste between April and August 2026, more than 2.5 times the entire 2025 total.

Water is part of the tourism footprint too

Tourism's environmental footprint is also much bigger than litter.

Niti Aayog's work on sustainable tourism in the Indian Himalayan Region highlights pressures involving water consumption, groundwater extraction, energy, accommodation, transportation and solid waste.

That is why âhidden gemâ is not necessarily synonymous with âsustainable destination.â

A small community may have a beautiful landscape but limited sewage treatment, parking, waste collection, medical facilities or water supply.

Goa shows that even beaches have a limit

The carrying-capacity question is not confined to the Himalayas. Goa recorded 10.8 million tourist arrivals in 2025, according to the state's tourism department.

An assessment placed before the National Green Tribunal found that, using a criterion of 10 square metres per visitor, carrying capacity was exceeded at beaches including Palolem, Agonda, Siridao, Vainguinim and Coco Beach.

The problem is therefore not âInstagram versus tourism.â It is tourism growth versus destination capacity.

The cost nobody sees on the reel

The local economy has something to gainâand lose

It would be simplistic to portray viral tourism as entirely destructive. A formerly overlooked destination gaining attention can mean more customers for homestays, restaurants, taxis, guides, artisans and small retailers.

But benefits are not automatically distributed equally.

If visitor numbers rise faster than local capacity, residents can face congestion, waste, water stress, rising costs and disruption to everyday life. Meanwhile, businesses may become increasingly dependent on a tourism boom they did not necessarily create or control.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

From viral tourism to responsible discovery

Indiaâs tourism challenge is therefore no longer simply about attracting visitors, but about distributing them intelligently.

As Joshi puts it, âDigital platforms can be used to distribute demand by making credible, attractive alternatives discoverable rather than concentrating everyone on the same few locations.â

Destinations, he argues, must plan for demand rather than chase it. âThe objective should not be to make destinations less popular, but to make tourism growth more manageable, more geographically distributed and more valuable to the communities that host it.â

World.title: 'Marriage does not advance a child’s age': Delhi HC rejects Muslim personal law defence in POCSO case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has refused to quash a POCSO case against a man who married a 16-year-old girl, holding that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot shield an adult from prosecution for sexual intercourse with a wife below 18.

Justice Sanjeev Narula said the statutory age of 18 under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) cannot be replaced by the concept of puberty under personal law. âPut simply, marriage does not advance a childâs age. A person who is sixteen before the ceremony remains sixteen afterwards," he said, as quoted by ANI.

The court was dealing with a petition filed by Bilal and another seeking quashing of FIR No. 189/2026 registered at Darya Ganj Police Station under Section 64(1) of the BNS and Section 6 of the

. The petitioners had also sought disciplinary action against police officials and compensation for alleged false implication and harassment.

According to the judgment, the girl was born on September 19, 2008, and married Bilal on December 20, 2024, when she was 16 years and three months old. Bilal was born on January 1, 1997 and was nearly 28 at the time. The couple subsequently lived together and the girl became pregnant. By May 2026, she was around eight months pregnant. Her age came to the notice of authorities when she visited a government hospital during her pregnancy.





The foetus later died in utero and the girl delivered a stillborn child on June 6, 2026. The judgment records that an order was subsequently obtained from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate for exhumation of the child for DNA profiling and collection of evidence.

The FIR was not based on an allegation made by the girl herself. She maintained that the marriage had taken place with the consent of both families, that she had married of her own free will and that physical relations began after the marriage.

She also supported Bilal during his bail proceedings and expressed a desire to have him by her side during her pregnancy.

The petitioners argued that under Muslim personal law, a Muslim of sound mind who has attained puberty is competent to marry and that, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, puberty is presumed after the age of 15. They contended that since the girl had attained puberty before the nikah, the marriage was valid and the subsequent sexual relationship could not attract criminal liability.

The High Court rejected the argument, observing, âPersonal law may determine whether a marriage has been contracted and the civil consequences that follow. It cannot supply an exception to a criminal law where Parliament has provided none."

The court clarified that it was not deciding whether the nikah was valid, void or voidable. Even if the marriage were assumed to be valid, it said, that would not take sexual intercourse with a person below 18 outside the scope of POCSO or the BNS.

The court also rejected the argument that the girl's consent or the absence of force and coercion could take the case outside POCSO.

âPOCSO does not confer such a power upon the child, her parents, or the Court,â it observed.

The court further said that the age difference between the couple did not by itself establish guilt, but was relevant while considering whether the court should exercise its exceptional jurisdiction to terminate a POCSO prosecution at the threshold.

The HC also rejected the argument that the FIR was unsustainable because neither the girl nor her family had approached the police, adding in this case, once doctors learnt that the pregnant patient was below 18, the statutory reporting mechanism was triggered, the court said.

The court also rejected the petitioners' reliance on constitutional freedoms under Articles 21, 25 and 26, holding that they could not create an exception to a generally applicable penal law enacted for the protection of children.

âConstitutional liberty protects choice; it does not create an exception to POCSO or the BNS,â the judgment said.

The court cautioned against an interpretation that would effectively introduce a marital exception into POCSO for children below 18.

Justice Narula added that, âThe statutory protection would then depend not upon the age of the child, but upon whether a marriage had been arranged before the sexual relationship was discovered.

That would turn the legislation on its head."

âThe conclusion is narrower: a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, by reason of that status alone, confer immunity from POCSO or BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time. Any other view would create, through judicial decision, an exception which Parliament has expressly excluded,â he added.

The court acknowledged that individual cases may involve âaffection rather than violence, and relationships rather than predationâ, but said such circumstances could not permit courts to rewrite the statutory definition of an offence.

Dismissing the petition, the High Court held that a marriage claimed to be valid under Muslim personal law cannot, merely because of that status, confer immunity from POCSO or the BNS for sexual intercourse with a wife who was below 18 at the relevant time.

World.title: Kapil Sibal alleges ‘unilateral’ EC decisions, seeks action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha member

on Sunday escalated the political row over the

's Special Intensive Revision (SIR), accusing chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of taking "unilateral decisions" and demanding his removal from office.

Sibal also urged the

to examine the Election Commission's records, dissent notes and orders issued during the period under question, and consider nullifying elections conducted during the 10-month period he referred to.

The former Union minister's remarks came amid a controversy over internal objections raised by election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi regarding decisions related to electoral rolls, the EC's IT systems and the SIR exercise.

Sibal alleges unilateral decision-making

According to Sibal, the Election Commission's own statement issued on Saturday acknowledged that decisions had not been taken unanimously over the past several months. He alleged that Kumar had taken decisions "unilaterally" rather than through the full three-member Commission.

Sibal claimed that Commission meetings were conducted without agendas being circulated or minutes being recorded, preventing the other commissioners from reviewing or commenting on decisions.





He said the alleged practices covered 10 months, including elections held in Bihar in June 2025 and West Bengal in April.

The allegations follow a report by The Indian Express, which said Sandhu and Joshi had formally raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders that they said were issued without their knowledge.

Sibal also alleged that decisions concerning additions and deletions of voters were centralised in Delhi through ECI NET under Seema Khanna, who managed its operations, instead of being handled by statutory Electoral Registration Officers.

He demanded that an FIR be registered against Khanna and that she be arrested, arguing that unlike the CEC, she does not have statutory immunity from criminal prosecution.

Sibal also alleged that changes were made to Form 6, used for new voter registration, requiring details of parents or grandparents without the central government issuing the required notification.

EC responds to concerns over SIR and electoral rolls

The Election Commission on Saturday announced several decisions addressing issues that Sandhu and Joshi had raised in their internal communications.

On Form 6, the EC said the additional declaration requiring new voters to provide details of their own or their parents' or grandparents' entries in the electoral roll from the previous SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.

It said the additional requirement was specific to the SIR exercise and that regular statutory forms would continue to be used outside an SIR.

On access to electoral-roll databases, the EC said field officers have role-based access to ECINET according to their statutory powers.

It also announced a review by a committee headed by a senior deputy election commissioner and including an independent IIT or IIIT expert to "double-check" the system's compliance with election laws and rules.

The Commission further said agendas for all meetings would be circulated in advance and minutes issued, while directions issued by commissioners to EC officers would be complied with.

On the IT division, the EC said disputed changes in the distribution of work were never implemented after Sandhu and Joshi intervened, and that oversight of the division by the deputy election commissioner was never withdrawn.

Sibal, however, claimed that the alleged irregularities meant elections conducted from Bihar through West Bengal during the period were "illegal". He called on the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter and consider whether recent elections should be annulled.

The opposition has also demanded Kumar's removal and an independent review of decisions and electoral-roll changes made during his tenure.

World.title: 'Protests happening across country': Priyanka Gandhi says CEC Gyanesh Kumar should resign 'now'
World.content:

âNot only do they have party leanings, but they are actively propagating those parties. How can they run fair elections?â she added.

âThere are protests in the whole country... In every district, we have protested against him. In Delhi, there have been protests,â Priyanka said.

World.title: Mamata AITC leader Kunal Ghosh attacked again, second time in 24 hours
World.content:
Beleghata MLA Kunal Ghosh was attacked on Sunday (September 27, 2026) and his vehicle was damaged by unidentified miscreants. This was the second attack on the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (AITC) leader in the past 24 hours. Mr. Ghosh was attacked at Uttarpara in Hooghly district on Saturday when he was on the way to attend a meeting of former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee.

The vehicle in which the MLA was travelling was destroyed both on Saturday (September 26) and Sunday (September 27). The Mamata Banerjee loyalist claimed he was certain that there was an attempt on his life so that he could be silenced. Mr. Ghosh is not only one of the most vocal critics of the Bharatiya Janata Party but also the MPs and MLAs who have rebelled against Mamata Banerjee.

“Today I was once again the target of an attempted murder. It all happened in the city of Kolkata, in broad daylight and on a Sunday, when I was on my way to attend a programme as an MLA I was attacked. They were armed; they smashed the car window and tried to drag me out, brandishing revolvers. My security personnel had to draw their weapons,” Mr. Ghosh said.

The journalist-turned-politician went to the Narkeldanga police station with the damaged car and lodged a formal complaint. The video shared by Mr. Ghosh revealed that several motorbikes where the riders had covered their faces with either helmet or masks were following his vehicle.

“Hundred per cent BJP is involved in the attack. BJP is certainly involved, and the police are inactive; we will have to see who else is implicated... What do they want? Do they want my dead body? Until I am dead, they will never be able to force me to change my stance,” the MLA said.

Appeal to Governor

Mamata AITC leader Abhishek Banerjee condemned the attack on the party MLA. Mr. Banerjee appealed to Governor R. N. Ravi to immediately intervene and speak to the Director General of West Bengal Police and the Commissioner of Police, Kolkata.

“Every perpetrator must be identified and brought to justice and this cycle of violence and intimidation must stop. Armed goons have targeted and harassed an elected representative, allegedly because he has refused to change sides,” Mr. Banerjee said. The Trinamool leader said the people of Bengal deserve peace and political violence, irrespective of who was behind it, had no place in a democracy.

BJP leader Sukanata Majumdar said the attack had nothing do with his party and the attack was a result of factionalisation in the Trinamool Congress.

World.title: Free health check-up camp for 110 women pourakarmikas
World.content:
A free comprehensive health check-up camp was organised for 110 women pourakarmikas of Zone 9 of the Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) in association with Dr. Jyothi’s Healthcare Hospital on Rajkumar Road here on Sunday.

MCC Commissioner Savita M.K. inaugurated the camp.

As part of the initiative aimed at safeguarding the health of women sanitation workers, a range of medical tests worth around ₹5,000 were conducted free of cost. The tests included complete haemogram, renal and liver function tests, lipid profile, random blood sugar, thyroid function test, HbA1c, Pap smear and ECG.

The beneficiaries were also provided consultations with a gynaecologist and a physician.

Dr. Jyothi, chief doctor of the hospital, personally examined all 110 pourakarmikas and provided individual counselling and necessary health advice.

Environmental Engineer of Zone 9 Lokeshwari, Zonal Development Officer Harshiya Taranam, health inspectors Prabhakar, Sahana and Shruthi, and other MCC staff were present.

The Commissioner appreciated the doctors, nursing and administrative staff for organising the health camp.

World.title: Phase 2 projects of Amrit Bharat Station Scheme at Mangaluru Junction lay stress on passenger comfort, accessibility, and aesthetics
World.content:
Phase 2 works of Amrit Bharat Station Scheme (ABSS) which are fast-progressing at the Mangaluru Junction Railway Station have laid stress on passenger comfort, accessibility, aesthetics and modern station facilities.

A sleeping pod facility on the first floor has been completed, providing an additional accommodation facility for passengers. The porch pillar work has been completed.

Station façade improvement works, including cladding, are being executed. Extension of the station building is in progress.

The circulating area has undergone landscaping improvements, creating a more attractive and passenger-friendly environment. At Platforms 2 and 3, IRS-type platform shelters covering 11 bays are being provided. Six bays have already been completed, while roofing works are progressing on the remaining bays, the Palakkad Division of the Southern Railway said in a release.

The entrance arch structure has been completed, with painting works in progress, further enhancing the visual identity and entrance experience of the station. A compound wall along the approach road has also been completed. The extension of the station building roof towards the Netravathi End has been completed, improving weather protection and the overall appearance of the station.

Upgradation of the panel room, including cable concealment, wall cladding and flooring works, is also in progress. These improvements are aimed at providing a cleaner, safer and better-organised operational environment.

As part of the scheme’s emphasis on inclusive and accessible passenger facilities, dedicated Divyangjan parking, sinks and toilet facilities have been completed. A major six-metre-wide Foot over Bridge (FoB) is currently being constructed. It will provide improved connectivity and facilitate smoother movement of passengers within the station. Lifts at Platforms 1 and 2 are also being provided, with foundation and structural fabrication works completed.

In addition, reconstruction and repair works of Platform Numbers 2 and 3 are in progress, further strengthening the passenger infrastructure and improving the overall condition and functionality of the platforms.

The ongoing redevelopment at Mangaluru Junction brings together modern passenger amenities, improved circulation, enhanced accessibility, upgraded operational infrastructure and significant improvements in station aesthetics. With the works being implemented in a phased manner, the redevelopment is set to substantially improve the overall passenger experience and transform Mangaluru Junction into a more modern, accessible, comfortable and passenger-friendly railway station, while further strengthening its role as an important railway gateway to the coastal region of Karnataka, the Southern Railway said.

Phase 1 projects

Under Phase 1 of the ABSS works, substantial improvements have been undertaken to upgrade the existing station infrastructure. The porch and façade of the station building have been improved, giving the station a more welcoming and modern appearance. Development of the circulating area, provision of Automated Ticket Vending Machines (ATVMs), improvement of the booking office with modern display boards, and construction of a new waiting hall building are among the major passenger-oriented facilities taken up under the scheme.

Meanwhile, this station will come under South Western Railway from October 1.

World.title: Kanaka Durga Temple atop Indrakeeladri invites applications for Dasara cultural programmes
World.content:
The Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam has invited applications from eligible artistes and cultural troupes interested in presenting devotional music, dance, and other cultural programmes during the Dasara Sarannavarathri festivities at Indrakeeladri from October 11 to 20.

Temple Executive Officer V.K. Seena Nayak said the programmes would be organised as part of the festivities. Application forms are available on the temple’s official website. Applicants can download the form, fill in the required details and submit it to the temple authorities. The last date for the applications to reach the temple is October 5. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered, he said.

As per the temple rules, a maximum of six artistes will be permitted for each troupe, comprising the main artiste and five accompanying artistes. The same six members alone will be permitted as a group for darshan of the presiding deity.

Applicants have to enclose copies of certificates relating to diplomas, degrees or postgraduate qualifications in fine arts, details of their experience in the respective art form, newspaper clippings of earlier performances, photographs and appreciation certificates.

The main artiste must also submit a copy of the first page of the bank passbook, clearly showing the account number and IFSC code, along with the Aadhaar number and mobile phone number. Completed applications may be sent by post or submitted in person at the temple office. They may also be emailed to endow-eosdmsd@gov.in, he said.

The artistes proficient in classical music, Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam, Harikatha, Bhakti Ranjani, bhajans, Burrakatha, Kolatam, drama and other traditional art forms can apply. For further details regarding the rules and application process, applicants may contact the temple’s toll-free number 1800 425 9099, he added.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Sarvesh Kushare, Ancy Sojan clinch silver medals in men's high jump and women's long jump, respectively
World.content:
India’s Sarvesh Kushare and Ancy Sojan led for most of their respective men’s high jump and women’s long jump finals before settling for the silver medals, while Parul Chaudhary took home the women’s 3000m steeplechase bronze at the Asian Games in Nagoya on Sunday (September 27, 2026).

India’s squash campaign at the Asian Games ended with two silver medals, with Abhay Singh and teenage sensation Anahat Singh finishing runners-up in their respective singles finals. Abhay went down 3-0 to Malaysia’s Ng Eain Yow in the men’s final, while 18-year-old Anahat also settled for silver after losing 3-0 to Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam in the women’s title clash.

Also read | Indian kabaddi teams dominate with double gold

India endured a disappointing day in badminton at the Asian Games, with teenage sensation Unnati Hooda bowing out after a 16-21, 21-14, 17-21 quarterfinal loss to Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi, while women’s doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand also exited after losing 18-21, 9-21 to Malaysia’s Pearly Tan and Thinaah Muralitharan. Mixed doubles pair Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto completed the Indian exits, going down 14-21, 21-18, 18-21 to China’s world No. 1 Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dongping.
